A typical household's electricity contract is a few kilowatts, so 24 megawatts means one building using as much power as several thousand homes. Here's the thing about designing a data center: the biggest factor isn't the structure or the look. It's heat. How do you get rid of the heat the servers give off? Until now, the standard approach has been air cooling, with big air-conditioning systems blowing cold air up from under the floor. But servers for generative AI give off heat on a completely different scale, so you need liquid cooling, which circulates coolant directly through the servers. I think KIX15 supports both air and liquid cooling because no one can be sure which will be in greater demand by 2028. The other point is base isolation. What's inside isn't people, it's servers. But if they shake and stop in an earthquake, the services running on them stop too. From base isolation that protects human lives to base isolation that protects data. It feels like we've entered an era where the role of buildings is slowly changing.
briefing: MCDR is a 50-50 joint venture between Mitsubishi Corporation and US-based Digital Realty. Its KIX Campus is located in the Saito area, and KIX15 is the fifth building there. After it opens, the company will have 10 sites in Japan totaling about 220 MW
Cooling is a hybrid of air and liquid cooling. The main target users are hyperscalers, cloud providers and AI companies
Service is scheduled to start in the fourth quarter of 2028 (Cloud Watch)

hojosen.title: Data centers as architecture
hojosen.body: Data centers need a lot of power and cooling equipment relative to their floor area, and equipment accounts for much of the construction cost. Sites are chosen for stable ground, proximity to transmission lines and substations, and low flood risk. In the Tokyo area they are clustering in Inzai, Chiba Prefecture, and in the Kansai region in Saito (Ibaraki and Minoh). Base isolation is becoming standard for data centers in Japan.

hojosen.title: Liquid cooling as a turning point
hojosen.body: GPU servers for generative AI give off several times more heat per rack than conventional servers, and air cooling can no longer keep up. Liquid cooling, which circulates coolant directly to the heat-generating parts of the servers, requires piping and leak protection to be built into the building from the design stage, and it is changing the design requirements for data center buildings.

stories.title: 国交省が「住宅の維持保全・流通」の制度検討会を初開催 直した家が正しく値段のつく市場へ
stories.summary: 国交省は10月8日、「住宅の維持保全・流通に関する制度検討会」の初会合を開催。新築価格高騰を背景に、質の高い既存住宅が適正に評価される市場の仕組みを議論します。
body: 国土交通省は10月8日、「住宅の維持保全・流通に関する制度検討会」の初会合を東京・虎ノ門で開きました。10月2日の開催案内によると、テーマは「消費者に望まれる住宅の維持保全を考える」。住宅の品質や性能を維持保全するよう促す市場の枠組みと、既存住宅の買主が安心して取引できる環境整備の方策を議論します。会合は非公開で、議事は「現状と課題及び検討の方向性」の提示と意見交換でした。
ハウジング・トリビューン（ハウジングトゥデイ）によると、背景にあるのは新築住宅の価格高騰と着工戸数の減少です。質の高い既存住宅が適正に評価され、安心して取引・継承される市場環境をつくることを目指し、初会合では建物の品質・性能や維持保全の実施状況を市場で適切に評価する枠組みづくりの方向性が示されました。
国交省はこの週、10月7日に長期修繕計画作成ガイドラインの見直し検討会も立ち上げています。マンションの修繕と戸建てを含む住宅の維持保全、その両方で「建てた後にどう手入れし、それをどう価値として認めるか」を制度の側から問い直す動きが同時に始まった形です。
stories.commentary: 取り壊される家の平均築年数は、日本が32年、アメリカが67年、イギリスが81年。放送でも話した国交省の推計です。日本の家が短命なのは木造だからだけじゃなくて、家が「住む場所」から「資産」に変わったときに、古い家を直して使い続ける文化が育たなかったからだと僕は思っています。今回の検討会が面白いのは、「直したこと」を市場でどう評価するかを正面から扱う点です。たとえば断熱改修をして、屋根と外壁を直して、記録を残した家と、何もしていない築30年の家。いまの中古市場では、この2軒の値段がほとんど変わらないことがあるんです。だから手入れをする動機が湧かない。いま僕が関わっている小さな増築の案件でも、長期優良住宅の認定を維持できるかを評価機関と区に確認するところから始まりました。手入れの記録が制度の中で価値になる経路は、まだ細いんです。皆さんの実家は、直した履歴が残っていますか。建てる競争から、使い続ける競争へ。そういう時代に入ったんだと思います。
briefing: 第1回会合は10月8日10時〜12時、虎ノ門の会議室で開催。会議は非公開で、冒頭のみカメラ撮影可（国交省開催案内）
同じ週の10月7日には「長期修繕計画作成ガイドラインの見直し等に関する検討会」の第1回も開催。マンション側の修繕計画・修繕積立金の見直しを議論
国交省推計の滅失住宅の平均築後年数は日本32.1年、米国66.6年、英国80.6年（Sho建築士が10月5日の放送で引用）

hojosen.title: 既存住宅の評価と制度
hojosen.body: 日本では建物の価値を築年数で一律に減価する慣行が強く、木造戸建ては20〜25年で建物価格がほぼゼロと査定されることが多いとされてきました。国交省は2010年代から既存住宅の性能評価、インスペクション（建物状況調査）、長期優良住宅化リフォームなどの制度を整えてきましたが、市場価格に反映される仕組みはまだ限定的です。

hojosen.title: 新築価格高騰という背景
hojosen.body: 建設費と地価の上昇で新築の取得が難しくなり、既存住宅の活用に政策の重心が移っています。国交省は空き家を改修して賃貸する事業者への低利融資（2027年度開始予定）や、住宅ローン減税の既存住宅優遇なども進めており、今回の検討会はその「評価の物差し」をつくる役割です。

en.title: Japan's housing ministry launches panel on a market where well-kept homes get fair prices
en.summary: On Oct 8, Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) held the first meeting of a study group on housing maintenance and resale. Against the backdrop of soaring new-home prices, it will discuss market mechanisms that properly value high-quality existing homes.
body: Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) held the first meeting of its Study Group on Systems for the Maintenance and Distribution of Housing on Oct 8 in Toranomon, Tokyo. According to the meeting notice issued on Oct 2, the theme was "thinking about the housing maintenance that consumers want." The group will discuss a market framework that encourages owners to maintain the quality and performance of their homes, and ways to create an environment where buyers of existing homes can purchase with confidence. The meeting was closed to the public, and the agenda consisted of a presentation on "the current situation, issues and direction of study" followed by an exchange of views.

According to Housing Tribune (Housing Today), the background is soaring prices for new homes and a decline in housing starts. The aim is to create a market in which high-quality existing homes are properly valued and can be bought, sold and passed on with confidence. At the first meeting, the ministry laid out a direction for building a framework in which the market properly evaluates a building's quality and performance and how well it has been maintained.

The same week, on Oct 7, MLIT also launched a study group to review its guidelines for preparing long-term repair plans, the schedules Japanese condominium associations use to plan major repairs. On both fronts, condominium repairs and the maintenance of housing including detached houses, the government has begun at the same time to rethink, at the level of policy, how homes are cared for after they're built and how that care is recognized as value.
en.commentary: The average age of homes when they're demolished is 32 years in Japan, 67 years in the US and 81 years in the UK. Those are MLIT estimates I mentioned on my show. I don't think Japanese homes are short-lived just because they're built of wood. I think it's because, as homes turned from "places to live" into "assets," a culture of repairing old houses and continuing to use them never took root. What's interesting about this study group is that it tackles head-on the question of how the market should value the fact that a home has been fixed. Picture two houses, both 30 years old. One has had insulation upgrades, a new roof and repaired exterior walls, with records kept. The other has had nothing done. In today's resale market, those two can sell for almost the same price. So there's no incentive to take care of a home. Even on a small extension project I'm involved in right now, the first step was checking with the evaluation agency and the ward office whether the house could keep its Long-Life Quality Housing certification, a national label for durable, well-maintained homes. The path for maintenance records to become value within the system is still narrow. Does your parents' house have a record of the repairs it's had? From a competition to build to a competition to keep using. I think that's the era we've entered.
briefing: The first meeting was held on Oct 8 from 10 a.m. to noon in a meeting room in Toranomon. It was closed to the public, with cameras allowed only at the opening (MLIT meeting notice)

On Oct 7 of the same week, the first meeting of the Study Group on Revising the Guidelines for Preparing Long-Term Repair Plans was also held, discussing revisions to condominium repair plans and repair reserve funds
MLIT estimates put the average age of demolished homes at 32.1 years in Japan, 66.6 years in the US and 80.6 years in the UK (cited by Sho, Architect on his Oct 5 show)

hojosen.title: How existing homes are valued
hojosen.body: In Japan, the custom of depreciating a building's value uniformly by its age has been strong, and wooden detached houses have often been appraised as having almost no building value after 20 to 25 years. Since the 2010s, MLIT has put in place systems such as performance evaluations for existing homes, inspections (building condition surveys) and renovation programs to bring homes up to Long-Life Quality Housing standards, but mechanisms that carry through to market prices are still limited.

hojosen.title: The backdrop of soaring new-home prices
hojosen.body: Rising construction costs and land prices have made new homes harder to buy, and the focus of policy is shifting toward making use of existing homes. MLIT is also moving ahead with low-interest loans for operators that renovate vacant houses to rent out (planned to start in fiscal 2027) and with more favorable mortgage tax breaks for existing homes. This study group's role is to create the yardstick for valuing them.

stories.title: 名古屋・金山の新劇場はPFIで2035年度開業へ 2100席と1400席、約580億円
stories.summary: 名古屋市は10月1日、市民会館を建て替える新劇場整備運営事業の実施方針と要求水準書案を公表。BTO方式のPFIで2027年4月に入札公告、2035年度開業へ。
body: 名古屋市は10月1日、金山の日本特殊陶業市民会館（名古屋市民会館）を建て替える「新たな劇場整備運営事業」の実施方針と要求水準書案を公表しました。日刊建設工業新聞によると、事業方式は民間が設計・建設した施設を市に引き渡し運営も担うBTO方式のPFI。2027年4月にWTO対象の一般競争入札を公告し、9月に入札書と事業提案書を受け付け、12月に落札者を決める予定です。11月9日には現地見学会を開きます。
新しい劇場は延べ約3万900平方メートル。音楽公演を主眼にした2100席以上の第1ホールと、演劇・舞踊・伝統芸能を主眼にした1400席以上の第2ホールを設け、スタジオや練習室、共通ロビーを整備します。隣接する古沢公園の再整備も事業範囲に含まれます。設計・建設期間は2028年度から約7年間で、2035年度の開業が目標。概算事業費は約580億円です。
現在の市民会館は2027年度末でいったん閉館する予定です。中日新聞によると、2035年度の新劇場開館までの間、名古屋の大規模ホールが減る期間が生じます。隣接する商業施設「アスナル金山」も2028年2月までに解体し、高層の新しい複合施設を整備する計画が進んでいます。
stories.commentary: 2100席と1400席。この二つの数字は、ホールの設計で一番最初に決まる数字です。席数が決まると、舞台の間口と奥行き、客席の勾配、ロビーの広さ、必要なトイレの数まで連鎖して決まっていきます。だから基本計画の段階で「約2200席」「約1500席」だった数字が、今回の要求水準で「2100席以上」「1400席以上」に下がったのは、小さな変更に見えて建物の骨格に関わる話なんです。10月9日号の札幌の新MICE施設と同じで、ホールは柱のない大空間が要るので、1平方メートルあたりの建設費がどうしても高くなります。580億円を延べ3万900平方メートルで割ると、1平方メートルあたり約190万円。席数を少し減らしてでも事業費を抑えたい市の判断は、いまの建設費を考えればわかります。ただ、ホールは一度建てると50年使う建物です。2035年の名古屋に、2100席と1400席はちょうどいい大きさなんでしょうか。それを判断する材料を、皆さんは市のどこに求めますか。
briefing: 事業スケジュールは2027年4月入札公告、9月入札書・事業提案書受付、12月落札者決定、2028年度から設計・建設約7年、2035年度開業（日刊建設工業新聞）
2024年10月の基本計画案では第1ホール約2200席・第2ホール約1500席を見込んでいた。要求水準書案では2100席以上・1400席以上
現市民会館は2027年度末で閉館予定。隣接のアスナル金山は2028年2月までに解体し、民間と共同で複合施設を整備する計画（東海テレビ）

hojosen.title: BTO方式
hojosen.body: Build-Transfer-Operateの略。民間事業者が施設を建設し、完成後すぐに所有権を自治体に移したうえで、民間が長期間の維持管理・運営を担うPFIの一方式です。札幌の新MICEが採用するBT＋コンセッションとは、運営権の売却を伴わない点が異なります。

hojosen.title: 建て替え計画の経緯
hojosen.body: 名古屋市民会館は1972年開館。当初は改修で延命する案もありましたが、2021年に建て替え計画が見直され、5年間使えない期間が生じると報じられました。2022年に基本構想、2025年2月に基本計画を策定し、今回の実施方針公表でPFI手続きが本格化しました。

en.title: Nagoya's new Kanayama theater to open in fiscal 2035 via PFI, with 2,100- and 1,400-seat halls for ¥58 billion
en.summary: On Oct 1, Nagoya released the implementation policy and draft performance requirements for a new theater replacing its civic hall in Kanayama. Built under a BTO-type PFI, the project will be put out to tender in April 2027, aiming to open in fiscal 2035.
body: On Oct 1, the city of Nagoya released the implementation policy and draft performance requirements for its new theater development and operation project, which will replace the Nagoya Civic Hall in Kanayama, a major transit hub south of central Nagoya. The hall is currently known as Nihon Tokushu Toryo Shimin Kaikan under a naming-rights deal. According to the Nikkan Kensetsu Kogyo Shimbun, a construction industry newspaper, the project will use a BTO-type PFI (private finance initiative), in which a private company designs and builds the facility, hands it over to the city and also runs it. The city plans to announce an open tender covered by the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement in April 2027, accept bids and proposals in September and choose the winner in December. A site tour will be held on Nov 9.

The new theater will have a total floor area of about 30,900 m² (333,000 sq ft). It will include Hall 1, with 2,100 or more seats and designed mainly for music, and Hall 2, with 1,400 or more seats and designed mainly for theater, dance and traditional performing arts, along with studios, rehearsal rooms and a shared lobby. Redevelopment of the adjacent Furusawa Park is also part of the project. Design and construction will take about seven years from fiscal 2028, with the goal of opening in fiscal 2035. The estimated project cost is about ¥58 billion.

The current civic hall is scheduled to close at the end of fiscal 2027. According to the Chunichi Shimbun, Nagoya will have fewer large halls in the period until the new theater opens in fiscal 2035. Next door, the Asunal Kanayama shopping complex is also set to be demolished by February 2028, with plans moving forward for a new high-rise mixed-use complex.
en.commentary: Two thousand one hundred seats and 1,400 seats. These two numbers are the very first ones decided in designing a concert hall. Once the seat count is set, everything else follows in a chain: the width and depth of the stage, the rake of the seating, the size of the lobby, even how many restrooms you need. So the fact that the basic plan's figures of about 2,200 and about 1,500 seats have dropped to "2,100 or more" and "1,400 or more" in these requirements may look like a small change, but it touches the skeleton of the building. Just like the new MICE (meetings, incentives, conventions and exhibitions) facility in Sapporo we covered on Oct 9, a hall needs a large column-free space, so its construction cost per square meter is unavoidably high. Divide ¥58 billion by 30,900 m² (333,000 sq ft) and you get about ¥1.9 million per square meter. Given today's construction costs, I understand the city's decision to hold down the project cost even if it means a few fewer seats. But a hall is a building you use for 50 years once it's built. Are 2,100 and 1,400 seats the right size for Nagoya in 2035? And where in the city would you look for the information to judge that?
briefing: Schedule: tender announced April 2027, bids and proposals accepted in September, winner chosen in December, about seven years of design and construction from fiscal 2028, and opening in fiscal 2035 (Nikkan Kensetsu Kogyo Shimbun)
The draft basic plan of October 2024 projected about 2,200 seats for Hall 1 and about 1,500 for Hall 2. The draft performance requirements call for 2,100 or more and 1,400 or more

The current civic hall is scheduled to close at the end of fiscal 2027. The adjacent Asunal Kanayama is to be demolished by February 2028, with plans to develop a mixed-use complex jointly with private partners (Tokai TV)

hojosen.title: The BTO model
hojosen.body: BTO stands for Build-Transfer-Operate. It is a type of PFI in which a private company builds a facility, transfers ownership to the local government immediately on completion, and then handles maintenance and operation over a long period. It differs from the BT plus concession model used for Sapporo's new MICE facility in that it does not involve selling the operating rights.

hojosen.title: How the rebuild came about
hojosen.body: Nagoya Civic Hall opened in 1972. At first there was a plan to extend its life through renovation, but the rebuilding plan was revised in 2021, and it was reported that there would be a five-year period without the hall. The city drew up a basic concept in 2022 and a basic plan in February 2025, and with this release of the implementation policy, the PFI process is now fully underway.

stories.title: 西新宿五丁目南地区に34階・高さ約140mの再開発 新宿区が都市計画原案、32年度竣工へ
stories.summary: 新宿区が十二社通り沿い約0.6haの西新宿五丁目南地区再開発の都市計画原案を策定。34階・延べ約4万600㎡、2027年2月に都市計画決定、2032年度竣工へ。
body: 東京都新宿区は、十二社通り沿いの約0.6ヘクタールで計画が進む「西新宿五丁目南地区第一種市街地再開発事業」の都市計画原案をまとめました。建設通信新聞が10月8日に報じたもので、意見募集と住民説明会を経て11月に区の都市計画審議会へ報告し、都市計画案を策定。2027年1月に縦覧と意見書の受付を行い、同年2月の都市計画決定を目指します。
再開発ビルはRC造34階建て、延べ約4万600平方メートル、高さ約140メートル。下層部に商業施設と駐車場、中高層部に住宅を配置し、北側2カ所に広場を整備します。都営大江戸線・西新宿五丁目駅から北東約300メートル、JR新宿駅から北西約1.2キロの立地で、準備組合は2016年に設立、事業協力者は住友不動産です。
今後は2027年度に組合設立、2028年度に権利変換計画の認可と既存建物の解体、2029年度に建築工事着工、2032年度の竣工・入居開始を予定しています。西新宿五丁目では隣接する中央南地区や北地区でも住友不動産が関わる再開発が進んでおり、十二社通り沿いの高層化が一段と進みます。
stories.commentary: 新宿駅から西へ1.2キロ。十二社通りは、超高層のオフィス街と木造住宅の密集地が隣り合う、新宿の中でも境目のような場所です。ここ10年、この通り沿いでは住友不動産が関わる再開発が北から順に進んできました。今回の南地区は0.6ヘクタールで34階。面積だけ見れば小さいんですが、僕が注目するのは「北側2カ所の広場」です。木造密集地の再開発では、タワーを建てること以上に、消防車が入れる道と、火災時に逃げ込める空地をつくることが目的になります。高さ140メートルの建物は、言ってみれば広場をつくるための対価なんです。この地区は準備組合の設立が2016年。都市計画決定まで11年、竣工まで16年かかる計算になります。再開発というのは、建物を建てる時間より、人の合意を積み上げる時間のほうがずっと長い仕事です。皆さんの近所の「準備組合」の看板、いつから立っていますか。竣工・入居開始の目標は2032年度です。
briefing: 事業スケジュールは2026年度内（2027年2月）都市計画決定、2027年度組合設立、2028年度権利変換認可・解体、2029年度着工、2032年度竣工・入居（建設通信新聞）
用途は住宅・商業・駐車場。中高層部が住宅で、タワーマンション中心の構成。北側2カ所に広場を整備
隣接の西新宿五丁目中央南地区（組合施行）でも再開発が進み、西新宿五丁目北地区では高さ約151mのツインタワーの防災街区整備事業が計画されている

sources.name: 超高層マンション・超高層ビル

hojosen.title: 西新宿五丁目の再開発群
hojosen.body: 都営大江戸線・西新宿五丁目駅周辺は、新宿副都心の西側に広がる木造住宅密集地で、2010年代から北地区・中央南地区・南地区など複数の市街地再開発や防災街区整備事業が段階的に進んでいます。住友不動産が多くの地区で事業協力者や参加組合員を務め、十二社通り沿いが高層住宅街に変わりつつあります。

hojosen.title: 都市計画原案から着工まで
hojosen.body: 組合施行の市街地再開発では、都市計画決定→組合設立認可→権利変換計画認可→解体・着工という手順を踏みます。各段階で地権者の同意が必要で、都市計画決定から着工まで2〜3年、準備組合の設立から数えると10年以上かかる例が珍しくありません。

en.title: Shinjuku drafts plan for 34-story, 140 m redevelopment in Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome South, aiming for 2032
en.summary: Tokyo's Shinjuku Ward has drafted an urban plan for the Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome South redevelopment on about 0.6 hectares (1.5 acres) along Juniso-dori avenue. The 34-story, roughly 40,600 m² (437,000 sq ft) tower aims for an urban planning decision in February 2027 and completion in fiscal 2032.
body: Shinjuku Ward in Tokyo has put together a draft urban plan for the Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome South District Category 1 Urban Redevelopment Project, which covers about 0.6 hectares (1.5 acres) along Juniso-dori avenue. This type of project is a Japanese scheme in which landowners pool their plots to build a larger complex. The Kensetsu Tsushin Shimbun, a construction industry newspaper, reported on Oct 8 that after public comments and resident briefings, the plan will be reported to the ward's urban planning council in November and turned into a formal draft. The ward will put it on public display and accept written opinions in January 2027, aiming for an urban planning decision in February that year.

The redevelopment building will be a 34-story reinforced concrete tower with a total floor area of about 40,600 m² (437,000 sq ft) and a height of about 140 m (460 ft). Retail and parking will occupy the lower floors and housing the middle and upper floors, with two plazas on the north side. The site is about 300 m (980 ft) northeast of Nishi-Shinjuku-gochome Station on the Toei Oedo subway line and about 1.2 km (0.75 miles) northwest of JR Shinjuku Station. The preparatory association was formed in 2016, and Sumitomo Realty & Development is the project partner.

Going forward, the plan calls for the redevelopment association to be established in fiscal 2027; approval of the rights conversion plan, the step that swaps landowners' existing property for space in the new building, and demolition of existing buildings in fiscal 2028; start of construction in fiscal 2029; and completion and move-in in fiscal 2032. In Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome, redevelopments involving Sumitomo Realty are also underway in the neighboring Central South and North districts, further pushing high-rise development along Juniso-dori.
en.commentary: About 1.2 km (0.75 miles) west of Shinjuku Station. Juniso-dori is a kind of borderline in Shinjuku, a street where the skyscraper office district sits right next to a dense neighborhood of wooden houses. Over the past 10 years, redevelopments involving Sumitomo Realty have been moving along this street from north to south. This South district covers 0.6 hectares (1.5 acres) and gets a 34-story tower. By area alone it's small, but what I'm watching is the "two plazas on the north side." In redevelopments of dense wooden-house neighborhoods, the real goal, even more than building a tower, is to create roads that fire trucks can get into and open space where people can take refuge in a fire. The 140 m (460 ft) building is, in a sense, the price paid to create those plazas. The preparatory association for this district was formed in 2016. That means 11 years to the urban planning decision and 16 years to completion. Redevelopment is work where the time spent building agreement among people is far longer than the time spent building the building. In Japan, you often see a redevelopment "preparatory association" sign posted in a neighborhood long before anything gets built. If there's one in your neighborhood, how long has it been up? The target for completion and move-in is fiscal 2032.
briefing: Schedule: urban planning decision within fiscal 2026 (February 2027), association established in fiscal 2027, rights conversion approval and demolition in fiscal 2028, construction start in fiscal 2029, and completion and move-in in fiscal 2032 (Kensetsu Tsushin Shimbun)
Uses are housing, retail and parking. The middle and upper floors are housing, making it mainly a tower condominium. Two plazas will be built on the north side

Redevelopment is also underway in the adjacent Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome Central South District (association-led), and twin towers about 151 m (495 ft) tall are planned for the Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome North District under a disaster-prevention block improvement project, a scheme for rebuilding fire-prone neighborhoods

hojosen.title: Nishi-Shinjuku 5-chome's redevelopments
hojosen.body: The area around Nishi-Shinjuku-gochome Station on the Toei Oedo Line is a dense wooden-house district spreading west of the Shinjuku skyscraper district. Since the 2010s, several urban redevelopment and disaster-prevention block improvement projects, including the North, Central South and South districts, have moved forward in stages. Sumitomo Realty & Development serves as project partner or participating member in many of them, and Juniso-dori is turning into a street of high-rise housing.

hojosen.title: From draft plan to groundbreaking
hojosen.body: An association-led urban redevelopment project in Japan goes through a set sequence: urban planning decision, approval of the association, approval of the rights conversion plan, then demolition and construction. Each stage requires landowner consent, and it is not unusual for two to three years to pass from the urban planning decision to groundbreaking, or more than 10 years counting from the formation of the preparatory association.

stories.title: 続報：福岡・天神のパルコ街区再開発 総事業費1658億円の事業計画案 2027年3月着工へ
stories.summary: 新天町商店街商業協同組合などが天神二丁目南ブロック駅前東街区の事業計画案を策定。総事業費1658億円で、2027年3月着工・2031年12月完成を目指します。
body: 福岡市・天神の「天神二丁目南ブロック駅前東街区第一種市街地再開発事業」について、新天町商店街商業協同組合、新天町商店街公社、西日本鉄道、三菱UFJ信託銀行、三井住友銀行が事業計画案をまとめたと建設通信新聞が10月9日に報じました。対象面積は約1.5ヘクタール、総事業費は1658億200万円。2027年3月の着工、2031年12月の完成を目指し、事業期間は2034年3月までを予定しています。特定業務代行者は竹中工務店です。

9月14日号でお伝えした福岡市の公表では、再開発ビルは地下4階・地上22階建て、延べ約14万1000平方メートル、高さ約110メートルで、概算整備費は約1230億円でした。今回の事業計画案では延べ面積が14万1471平方メートルと示され、総事業費の内訳は本体工事費1175億1100万円、調査設計計画費51億1900万円、メルヘン地下通路整備費86億1900万円、土地整備費98億4700万円などです。地下2階から地上7階が商業、8階以上がオフィスとハイグレードホテルの構成です。
福岡市は9月の市議会で、東街区の設計・整備費を2025年度試算の約1000億円から約1230億円に増額したと報告していました。隣接する西街区（新天町側）は敷地約5900平方メートル・延べ約8万8000平方メートルで、2027年春ごろの解体着手、2030年代の完成を予定しています。
stories.commentary: 1658億円のうち、建物本体の工事費は1175億円。残りの約480億円が、設計や調査、地下通路、土地の整備といった「建物以外」の費用です。再開発というと高層ビルの姿ばかり目に入りますが、お金の内訳を見ると、通路や権利の整理に使う分がこれだけ大きいんです。注目したいのは「メルヘン地下通路」に86億円が計上されていること。天神地下街と西鉄福岡駅、パルコをつなぐ地下の動線は、地上のビルと同じくらい街の使い勝手を決めます。もうひとつ、1年前の試算は約1000億円、9月の市の報告で1230億円、今回の事業計画案で総額1658億円。数字の範囲が違うので単純比較はできませんが、建設費の上がり方を追う材料としては十分です。この規模の再開発は、組合、鉄道会社、信託銀行が一つの事業者になって進めます。商店街の店主さんたちが共同事業者として1658億円の計画を背負う。皆さんは、自分の街の商店街がこの判断を迫られたら、どう考えますか。
briefing: 事業者は新天町商店街商業協同組合、新天町商店街公社、三菱UFJ信託銀行、西日本鉄道、三井住友銀行。パルコ街区側の事業者にはパルコ、J.フロント都市開発も名を連ねる
再開発ビルの用途構成は地下2階〜地上7階が商業施設、8階以上がオフィスとハイグレードホテル
天神ビッグバンは福岡市が2015年に始めた都心再開発施策。航空法の高さ制限67mに対し、明治通り西側は約115mまで緩和されている
西街区（新天町側）は2027年春ごろに解体着手、2030年代の完成予定

hojosen.title: 特定業務代行者
hojosen.body: 市街地再開発組合などが、工事の施工や資金調達の一部を含む業務をまとめて委ねる民間事業者。ゼネコンが担うことが多く、組合側の事業リスクを引き受ける代わりに施工を担当します。竹中工務店は天神エリアで複数の再開発に関わっています。

hojosen.title: 天神ビッグバンの期限
hojosen.body: 福岡市の天神ビッグバンは国家戦略特区の規制緩和を使った建て替え促進策で、容積率や高さ制限の特例を受けるには竣工期限（当初2024年末、現在は2026年末に延長）があります。駅前東街区は2031年完成予定のため、特例の扱いは別の枠組みで整理される見通しです。

en.title: Update: Fukuoka's Tenjin Parco block redevelopment plan puts total cost at ¥165.8 billion
en.summary: A group led by the Shintencho shopping arcade has drawn up the project plan for a redevelopment in Tenjin, downtown Fukuoka. Total cost is ¥165.8 billion, with construction set to start in March 2027 and finish in December 2031.
body: A project plan has been drawn up for the Tenjin 2-chome South Block Station-Front East District Type 1 Urban Redevelopment Project in Tenjin, the main downtown and shopping district of Fukuoka, the largest city on the southern island of Kyushu. The construction trade paper Kensetsu Tsushin Shimbun reported on Oct 9 that the plan was put together by the Shintencho Shopping Arcade Commercial Cooperative, the Shintencho Shopping Arcade Corporation, Nishi-Nippon Railroad (Nishitetsu), Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation. The site covers about 1.5 hectares (3.7 acres), and the total project cost is ¥165.802 billion. Construction is to start in March 2027 and finish in December 2031, with the project period running through March 2034. Takenaka Corporation is the specified agent contractor, the builder that takes on part of the project on the landowners' behalf.

As we reported on Sep 14, the City of Fukuoka had announced a redevelopment building with four basement levels and 22 stories above ground, about 141,000 m² (1.52 million sq ft) of total floor area, a height of about 110 m (360 ft), and a rough construction cost of about ¥123 billion. The new project plan gives the total floor area as 141,471 m² (1.52 million sq ft). The total cost breaks down into ¥117.511 billion for the building itself, ¥5.119 billion for surveys, design and planning, ¥8.619 billion for the Meruhen underground passage, and ¥9.847 billion for land preparation, among other items. Retail will occupy the second basement level through the seventh floor, with offices and a high-end hotel on the eighth floor and above.

At the September session of the city council, Fukuoka reported that the design and construction cost for the East District had risen from about ¥100 billion in its fiscal 2025 estimate to about ¥123 billion. The neighboring West District, on the Shintencho side, has a site of about 5,900 m² (64,000 sq ft) and about 88,000 m² (950,000 sq ft) of total floor area. Demolition there is expected to begin around spring 2027, with completion sometime in the 2030s.
en.commentary: Of the ¥165.8 billion, the building itself accounts for ¥117.5 billion. The other roughly ¥48 billion goes to things that aren't the building: design, surveys, the underground passage and land preparation. When people hear redevelopment, they tend to picture the tower. But look at the breakdown and you see how much goes to passageways and to sorting out property rights. What caught my eye is the ¥8.6 billion set aside for the Meruhen underground passage. The underground routes linking the Tenjin Underground Shopping Mall, Nishitetsu Fukuoka Station and Parco shape how usable the area is just as much as the building above ground does. One more thing. A year ago the estimate was about ¥100 billion, the city's September report said ¥123 billion, and this project plan puts the total at ¥165.8 billion. Those numbers cover different things, so you can't compare them directly, but they're plenty to track how fast construction costs are rising. A redevelopment this size is carried out by a cooperative, a railway company and trust banks acting together as one developer. The shop owners of a shopping arcade are shouldering a ¥165.8 billion plan as co-developers. If the shopping street in your own town had to make this call, how would you think it through?
briefing: The developers are the Shintencho Shopping Arcade Commercial Cooperative, the Shintencho Shopping Arcade Corporation, Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking, Nishi-Nippon Railroad and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation. Parco and J.Front Urban Development are also listed among the developers on the Parco block side
In the redevelopment building, retail will fill the second basement level through the seventh floor, with offices and a high-end hotel on the eighth floor and above

Tenjin Big Bang is an urban redevelopment policy the City of Fukuoka launched in 2015. The aviation law caps building heights at 67 m (220 ft) because of the nearby airport, but on the west side of Meiji-dori avenue the cap has been relaxed to about 115 m (380 ft)
In the West District, on the Shintencho side, demolition is expected to begin around spring 2027, with completion sometime in the 2030s

hojosen.title: Specified agent contractors
hojosen.body: A specified agent contractor (tokutei gyomu daikosha) is a private company that an urban redevelopment association hands a bundle of work to, including construction and part of the financing. The role usually goes to a general contractor, which takes on some of the association's project risk in exchange for building the project. Takenaka Corporation is involved in several redevelopments in the Tenjin area.

hojosen.title: The Tenjin Big Bang deadline
hojosen.body: Fukuoka's Tenjin Big Bang uses the deregulation available in a National Strategic Special Zone to encourage rebuilding. To qualify for exceptions on floor area ratio (FAR) and height limits, buildings must be completed by a deadline, originally the end of 2024 and now extended to the end of 2026. Because the Station-Front East District is due to be finished in 2031, its exceptions are expected to be handled under a separate framework.

stories.title: プリツカー賞の建築家・山本理顕氏が横浜市長選に立候補 「住む権利の保障」を掲げ18日投開票
stories.summary: 2024年プリツカー賞受賞の建築家・山本理顕氏（81）が横浜市長選に無所属で立候補。住む権利の保障や「地域社会圏」構想を掲げます。投開票は10月18日です。
body: 建築家の山本理顕氏（81）が、10月4日に告示された横浜市長選挙に無所属で立候補しました。山本氏は横須賀美術館や公立はこだて未来大学などを手がけ、2024年に「建築界のノーベル賞」と呼ばれるプリツカー賞を受賞しています。今回の市長選は、職員へのパワハラ問題で前市長が8月に辞職したことに伴うもので、前市長を含む7人が立候補しました。投開票は10月18日です。
タウンニュースによると、山本氏は届け出後の会見で「安全で快適な住宅に住む権利の保障」を主張。一つの町内会を「地域社会圏」と位置づけ、子どもや高齢者の支援、行政窓口、カフェなどを集めた町内会サロンの設置、公共交通網の充実、観光収入の増加、老朽化した市営住宅の整備などを掲げました。日経クロステックも「快適に住める権利」の保護を訴えていると伝えています。
「地域社会圏」は、山本氏が建築家として長年提唱してきた考え方です。一つの住宅に一つの家族が閉じて住む「一住宅一家族」の仕組みを見直し、数百人規模の集まりで住まいと仕事、生活サービスを共有する住まい方を提案してきました。建築家が自身の理論を自治体の政策として掲げる形になります。
stories.commentary: 建築家が市長選に出る。候補者7人のうちの一人として、事実として受け止めたいと思います。僕がここで触れたいのは勝ち負けではなく、公約の中身が建築の理論そのものだという点です。「地域社会圏」は、山本さんが2010年代から本や展覧会で語ってきた構想で、要するに「家族単位で閉じた住宅を、もう少し開いて、ご近所の数百人で支え合う」という考え方です。たとえば玄関脇に小さな店や仕事場を持てる住宅、1階がみんなの居間になる集合住宅。これは設計の話であると同時に、町内会や行政窓口をどこに置くかという政策の話でもあります。建築家は普段、設計した建物の中でしかこの構想を試せません。それを市の制度側から試そうとするのが今回の立候補です。皆さんは、住まいの「開き方」を行政が決めることに、どんな可能性と心配を感じますか。横浜市長選の投開票は10月18日です。
briefing: 山本氏は1945年生まれ。1973年に山本理顕設計工場を設立。代表作に横須賀美術館、埼玉県立大学、公立はこだて未来大学など。横浜国立大学大学院でも教授を務めた
公約には、市内全住宅の耐震診断・地盤調査や、市民が無料で使えるミニバス・ミニタクシー網の構想、観光収入を約5000億円から1兆円へ拡大する目標も含まれる（公式サイト・選挙公報による）
市長選は前市長の8月27日の辞職表明を受けて実施。告示10月4日、期日前投票は10月5日〜17日、投開票10月18日

hojosen.title: 地域社会圏
hojosen.body: 山本理顕氏が提唱する住まいの構想。戦後の住宅政策が前提にしてきた「一住宅一家族」を見直し、500人程度の集まりを単位に、住宅の一部を開いて小さな店や仕事場、共用の居間を持ち、生活のサービスを分け合う考え方です。2010年代に書籍や展覧会で発表され、建築界で議論を呼びました。

hojosen.title: プリツカー賞と日本人
hojosen.body: プリツカー賞は1979年創設の国際建築賞。日本からは丹下健三、槇文彦、安藤忠雄、妹島和世と西沢立衛、伊東豊雄、坂茂、磯崎新らが受賞しており、2024年の山本理顕氏で日本人受賞者は9組目です。

en.title: Pritzker-winning architect Riken Yamamoto runs for mayor of Yokohama on a right to housing
en.summary: Riken Yamamoto, 81, the architect who won the 2024 Pritzker Prize, is running as an independent for mayor of Yokohama. His platform centers on a right to decent housing and his Local Community Area concept. Voting is on Oct 18.
body: Architect Riken Yamamoto, 81, has entered the Yokohama mayoral election as an independent. The official campaign began on Oct 4. Yamamoto designed the Yokosuka Museum of Art and Future University Hakodate, among other works, and in 2024 he won the Pritzker Prize, often called the Nobel Prize of architecture. The election was triggered by the previous mayor's resignation in August over a power harassment controversy involving city employees. Seven candidates are running, including the former mayor. Voting takes place on Oct 18.

According to the local paper Town News, Yamamoto said at a press conference after filing his candidacy that he would guarantee the right to live in safe, comfortable housing. He proposes treating each neighborhood association, the residents' groups found in neighborhoods across Japan, as a Local Community Area. His platform includes neighborhood association salons that bring together support for children and older people, government service counters and cafes, along with a stronger public transit network, more tourism revenue and upgrades to aging municipal housing. Nikkei Xtech also reported that he is calling for protection of the right to live comfortably.

The Local Community Area (chiiki shakai ken) is an idea Yamamoto has promoted for many years as an architect. It rethinks the one-house-one-family model, in which each household lives closed off in its own home, and proposes groups of a few hundred people sharing housing, work and everyday services. With this campaign, an architect is putting his own theory forward as city policy.
en.commentary: An architect is running for mayor. He's one of seven candidates, and I want to take that simply as a fact. What I want to talk about here isn't whether he wins or loses. It's that his platform is, at its core, architectural theory. The Local Community Area is a concept Yamamoto has been laying out in books and exhibitions since the 2010s. In short, it says: take homes that are closed around a single family, open them up a little, and let a few hundred neighbors support one another. Think of a house with a small shop or workspace next to the front door, or an apartment building whose ground floor works as everyone's living room. That's a design question, and at the same time a policy question about where neighborhood associations and government counters should go. Normally an architect can only test an idea like this inside the buildings he designs. This candidacy is an attempt to test it from the side of the city's own systems. What possibilities, and what worries, do you see in a city government deciding how our homes should open up? Voting in the Yokohama mayoral election is on Oct 18.
briefing: Yamamoto was born in 1945 and founded his office, Riken Yamamoto & Field Shop, in 1973. His major works include the Yokosuka Museum of Art, Saitama Prefectural University and Future University Hakodate. He has also taught as a professor at the graduate school of Yokohama National University

His pledges also include seismic assessments and ground surveys for every home in the city, a network of minibuses and mini-taxis that residents can ride for free, and a goal of growing tourism revenue from about ¥500 billion to ¥1 trillion (according to his official website and the election bulletin)
The election follows the previous mayor's announcement on Aug 27 that he would resign. The campaign officially opened on Oct 4, early voting runs Oct 5 to 17, and voting day is Oct 18

hojosen.title: The Local Community Area
hojosen.body: A housing concept proposed by Riken Yamamoto. It questions the one-house-one-family model that postwar Japanese housing policy took for granted. Instead, it takes a group of about 500 people as the basic unit, opens part of each home for a small shop, a workspace or a shared living room, and lets residents share everyday services. Yamamoto presented it in books and exhibitions in the 2010s, and it sparked debate in the architecture world.

hojosen.title: Japan and the Pritzker Prize
hojosen.body: The Pritzker Prize is an international architecture award founded in 1979. Japanese winners include Kenzo Tange, Fumihiko Maki, Tadao Ando, Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa, Toyo Ito, Shigeru Ban and Arata Isozaki. With Riken Yamamoto in 2024, Japan has produced nine winners (counting Sejima and Nishizawa as one).

stories.title: 続報：一級建築士の設計製図試験はあす10月11日 法令集持ち込み元年、学科合格7619人
stories.summary: 令和8年一級建築士「設計製図の試験」があす10月11日に実施。課題は「ホテル」、試験時間は6時間30分。今年から法令集を持ち込めます。合格発表は12月23日。
body: 令和8年の一級建築士試験「設計製図の試験」が、あす10月11日（日）に全国で行われます。9月24日号でお伝えしたとおり、今年の課題は「ホテル」。試験は11時から17時30分までの6時間30分で、その前の10時35分から注意事項の説明があります。合格発表は12月23日の予定です。
今年は製図試験に法令集を持ち込める最初の年です。建築技術教育普及センターの受験要領によると、使用できる法令集は2冊までで、付随する追録や訂正表は追加できます。学科の法規と同様、書き込みやインデックスには条件があり、当日の確認対象になります。
今年の学科試験は受験者2万9094人に対し合格者7619人、合格率26.2%で、前年の16.5%から大きく上がりました。総合資格学院によると、現在の出題形式になった平成21年以降で最も高い合格率です。製図試験には学科合格者のほか、過去2年以内の学科合格による受験者も加わります。
stories.commentary: あす、全国の試験会場で数千人が同じ「ホテル」を6時間半で描きます。放送でも話したんですが、僕は二級も一級も一発で受かりました。緊張は学科のほうが強くて、製図のときは受かる気ではいたけれど、挑戦者であるという気持ちだけは忘れずに臨んだ記憶があります。今年は法令集を手元に置ける初めての年。安心材料であると同時に、「確認しなかった」が通らなくなる年でもあります。条文が手元にあるのに見落とせば、知識不足ではなく手順の問題になります。だから僕が勧めるのは、法令集を開く場面をあらかじめ3つくらいに決めておくこと。エスキスの最初、プラン確定前、作図後のチェック。この3回以外は本を閉じる。そのほうが6時間半の配分が崩れません。もう一つ、放送で言ったことをここでも。合格率35%前後の試験に、人生を賭けないでください。受かっても落ちても、建築の仕事は続きます。あす受ける皆さんは、今夜のうちに法令集の付箋と製図道具をもう一度だけ確認して、早めに寝てください。
briefing: 製図試験の時間割は10時35分〜11時が注意事項の説明（25分）、11時〜17時30分が本試験（6時間30分）
学科試験の合格基準点は総得点94点。合格者の64.7%を20代が占めた（総合資格学院の分析による）
学科合格者は翌年・翌々年の製図試験も受けられる。製図試験は学科合格1回につき3回まで受験できる
製図試験の合格発表は12月23日（水）予定。合格すると建築士免許の登録手続きに進める

sources.name: 建築技術教育普及センター（公式）

hojosen.title: 学科の合格率が上がった背景
hojosen.body: 令和8年の学科試験は合格率26.2%で、前年比9.7ポイント上昇しました。合格基準点は当初の目安「概ね90点」から94点に上方補正されましたが、それでも合格者は7619人と近年で最多です。製図試験の受験者が増える分、相対評価の製図ではランク分けの競争が例年より厳しくなるという見方もあります。

hojosen.title: 製図試験の採点
hojosen.body: 設計製図の試験はランクI〜IVの4段階で評価され、ランクIのみ合格です。法規違反や要求室の欠落など致命的なミスはランクIVとなり、図面の出来にかかわらず不合格になります。法令集の持ち込みで、法規関連のミスの扱いが変わるかどうかが今年の注目点です。

stories.sourceName: 建築技術教育普及センター（公式）

en.title: Update: Design exam for Japan's top architect license is tomorrow, the first with code books allowed
en.summary: The 2026 design drafting exam for the first-class kenchikushi license, Japan's top architect license, takes place tomorrow, Oct 11. This year's brief is a hotel, the exam lasts 6 hours 30 minutes, and candidates may bring code books for the first time. Results come out Dec 23.
body: The 2026 design drafting exam for the first-class kenchikushi license, Japan's top architect license, which covers buildings of any size, will be held nationwide tomorrow, Sunday, Oct 11. It is the second stage of the licensing exam, after a written test, and candidates must produce a full building design on paper within the time limit. As we reported on Sep 24, this year's brief is a hotel. The exam runs from 11:00 to 17:30, a total of 6 hours 30 minutes, preceded by an explanation of the rules starting at 10:35. Results are scheduled for Dec 23.

This is the first year candidates can bring code books, compilations of building laws and regulations, into the drafting exam. According to the exam guidelines from the Japan Architectural Education and Information Center (JAEIC), the body that runs the exam, candidates may use up to two code books, and may add the supplements and errata sheets that come with them. As in the building regulations section of the written exam, there are rules on handwritten notes and index tabs, and books will be checked on the day.

This year 29,094 people took the written exam and 7,619 passed, a pass rate of 26.2%, sharply up from 16.5% the year before. According to Sogo Shikaku Gakuin, a major exam-prep school, that is the highest pass rate since the exam took its current format in 2009. Besides this year's written-exam passers, the drafting exam also includes candidates who passed the written exam within the past two years.
en.commentary: Tomorrow, several thousand people at exam sites across Japan will each draw the same hotel in six and a half hours. I mentioned this on my show, but I passed both the second-class and first-class exams on my first try. I was more nervous about the written exam. Going into the drafting exam I fully expected to pass, but I made a point of never forgetting that I was the challenger. This is the first year you can keep a code book at your desk. That's reassuring, but it also means "I didn't check" no longer works as an excuse. If the provision is right there and you still miss it, that's not a gap in knowledge. It's a problem with your process. So here's what I recommend: decide in advance on about three moments when you'll open the book. At the start of your esquisse, the rough planning sketch. Before you lock in the plan. And during your check after drawing. Outside those three, keep it closed. That way your six and a half hours won't fall apart. And one more thing I said on the show, which I'll repeat here. Don't bet your life on an exam with a pass rate of around 35%. Pass or fail, your work in architecture goes on. If you're sitting the exam tomorrow, check your code book tabs and drafting tools one last time tonight, and get to bed early.
briefing: The drafting exam schedule: 10:35 to 11:00 is an explanation of the rules (25 minutes), and 11:00 to 17:30 is the exam itself (6 hours 30 minutes)
The pass mark for the written exam was 94 points in total. People in their 20s made up 64.7% of those who passed (according to an analysis by Sogo Shikaku Gakuin)
Those who pass the written exam can also take the drafting exam in the following two years. Each written-exam pass allows up to three attempts at the drafting exam
Drafting exam results are scheduled for Wednesday, Dec 23. Those who pass can go on to register for their kenchikushi license

hojosen.title: Why the written pass rate jumped
hojosen.body: The 2026 written exam had a pass rate of 26.2%, up 9.7 percentage points from the year before. The pass mark was adjusted upward from the initial guideline of roughly 90 points to 94, yet 7,619 people still passed, the most in recent years. With more candidates sitting the drafting exam, which is graded on a relative basis, some expect competition for the top grade to be tougher than usual.

hojosen.title: How the drafting exam is graded
hojosen.body: The design drafting exam is graded on four ranks, I to IV, and only Rank I passes. Fatal mistakes such as a building code violation or a missing required room put a candidate in Rank IV, a fail no matter how good the drawings are. One thing to watch this year is whether allowing code books changes how code-related mistakes are treated.

stories.title: 「東京ミッドタウン日本橋」が竣工 高さ約284mの52階建て、グランドオープンは27年内
stories.summary: 三井不動産と野村不動産は10月8日、再開発「東京ミッドタウン日本橋」が9月30日に竣工したと発表。設計は日建設計、施工は清水建設JV。開業は2027年内です。
body: 三井不動産と野村不動産は10月8日、東京・日本橋一丁目中地区第一種市街地再開発事業の全体街区「東京ミッドタウン日本橋」が9月30日に竣工したと発表しました。中核となるC街区のタワーは地上52階・地下5階、高さ約284メートルで、日本橋駅に直結します。設計・監理は日建設計、施工は清水建設を代表とする共同企業体が担当しました。日本橋川周辺の再開発一帯「日本橋リバーウォーク」の第1弾プロジェクトと位置づけられています。
タワーの39〜47階にはヒルトン最上位ブランドのホテル「ウォルドーフ・アストリア東京日本橋」（197室）、48〜51階には賃貸住宅「ウォルドーフ・アストリア・レジデンス東京日本橋」（71戸）が入ります。5〜7階には約1600人を収容できるMICE施設、低層部と地下には約100区画・約2万平方メートルの商業ゾーンが配置されます。
竣工は建物の完成を指し、グランドオープンは2027年内の予定です。D街区の既存ビル「日本橋一丁目三井ビルディング」の改修完了をもって街区全体が完成する計画で、既存の「COREDO日本橋」は商業ゾーンの一部として改称・リニューアルされます。
stories.commentary: 「竣工」と「開業」が1年以上ずれるのはなぜか、気になった人もいると思います。竣工は建物の本体が完成して、検査を終えて建築主に引き渡される日のことです。その時点でホテルの客室も店舗の内装もまだ空っぽ。ここからテナントごとの内装工事、ホテルの什器や設備の搬入、スタッフの訓練が始まります。284メートルのビルを建てるのに約5年、建物を「使える状態」にするのにさらに1年というのが、この規模の複合ビルの時間感覚なんです。僕が注目しているのは、日本橋川との関係です。このエリアでは首都高の地下化が進んでいて、川の上を走る高架がなくなった後の日本橋が、この再開発の「正面」になる計画です。ビルの高さより、足元の川沿いがどう使われるかで評価が決まる建物だと思います。52階建てのタワーが日本橋に1棟増えた、という話ではなく、川を表に戻す街づくりの1棟目。そういう見方で、2027年の開業を待ちたいです。
briefing: C街区タワーの延べ面積は約37万4800平方メートル。高さ約284mは国内4位・東京都内2位の高さとされる
街区はA〜Dの4街区構成。商業ゾーンは約100区画・約2万平方メートルで、物販・飲食が出店予定
同日発表の「日本橋一丁目エネルギーセンター」（三井不動産とTEPCOエナジーパートナー）も9月30日に竣工し、10月1日から街区全体に電気・熱を供給。CO2排出量約25%削減を見込む
街区名称「東京ミッドタウン日本橋」は2026年4月21日に決定。六本木・日比谷・八重洲に続く4つ目の「ミッドタウン」

sources.name: 三井不動産（公式・PR TIMES）

hojosen.title: 日本橋リバーウォーク
hojosen.body: 三井不動産などが日本橋川沿いで進める複数の再開発を束ねたエリア名称。首都高速の日本橋区間の地下化と合わせ、川沿いに歩行者空間や親水空間をつくる構想で、東京ミッドタウン日本橋はその第1弾にあたります。

hojosen.title: 竣工から開業までの1年
hojosen.body: 大型複合ビルでは、建物本体の竣工後にテナントの内装工事（B工事・C工事）やホテルの開業準備が続くため、竣工から半年〜1年以上あけてグランドオープンするのが一般的です。東京ミッドタウン八重洲も2022年8月竣工、2023年3月開業でした。

stories.sourceName: 三井不動産（公式・PR TIMES）

en.title: Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi, a 52-story, 284 m (930 ft) tower, is completed ahead of a 2027 opening
en.summary: Mitsui Fudosan and Nomura Real Estate Development announced on Oct 8 that Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi, a redevelopment in Tokyo's historic Nihonbashi district, was completed on Sep 30. Nikken Sekkei designed it, a Shimizu-led joint venture built it, and the grand opening is set for 2027.
body: Mitsui Fudosan and Nomura Real Estate Development announced on Oct 8 that Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi, the full development of the Nihonbashi 1-chome Central District Type 1 Urban Redevelopment Project, was completed on Sep 30. Nihonbashi is a historic commercial district near Tokyo Station, named after the old bridge at its center. The centerpiece, the tower on Block C, rises 52 stories above ground with five basement levels and stands about 284 m (930 ft) tall, with a direct connection to Nihonbashi Station. Nikken Sekkei handled design and supervision, and a joint venture led by Shimizu Corporation built it. The project is positioned as the first phase of Nihonbashi Riverwalk, the name for the cluster of redevelopments along the Nihonbashi River.

Floors 39 to 47 of the tower will house the Waldorf Astoria Tokyo Nihonbashi (197 rooms), from Hilton's top-tier brand, and floors 48 to 51 will hold the Waldorf Astoria Residences Tokyo Nihonbashi, with 71 rental apartments. Floors 5 to 7 will contain a MICE facility (for meetings, incentive travel, conferences and exhibitions) that can hold about 1,600 people. The lower floors and basement will have a retail zone of about 100 shops covering about 20,000 m² (215,000 sq ft).

Completion means the building itself is finished; the grand opening is planned for sometime in 2027. The district as a whole will be complete once renovation of the existing Nihonbashi 1-chome Mitsui Building on Block D is finished, and the existing COREDO Nihonbashi shopping center will be renamed and renovated as part of the retail zone.
en.commentary: Some of you may be wondering why completion and opening are more than a year apart. Completion is the day the building itself is finished, passes its inspections and is handed over to the owner. At that point the hotel rooms and the shops are still empty shells. Only then do the tenants' interior fit-outs begin, along with moving in the hotel's furniture and equipment and training the staff. About five years to build a 284 m tower, then another year to make it usable: that's the sense of time for a mixed-use building of this size. What I'm watching is its relationship with the Nihonbashi River. In this area, the elevated Metropolitan Expressway that runs above the river is being moved underground, and once that overpass is gone, the plan is for the riverside to become the front of this redevelopment. I think this building will be judged less by its height than by how the riverside at its feet gets used. This isn't just one more 52-story tower in Nihonbashi. It's the first building in a plan to turn the city back to face its river. That's how I'd like to look at it as we wait for the 2027 opening.
briefing: The Block C tower has a total floor area of about 374,800 m² (4.03 million sq ft). Its height of about 284 m is said to rank fourth in Japan and second in Tokyo
The development is made up of four blocks, A through D. The retail zone covers about 100 shops and about 20,000 m² (215,000 sq ft), with stores and restaurants planned

The Nihonbashi 1-chome Energy Center (Mitsui Fudosan and TEPCO Energy Partner), announced the same day, was also completed on Sep 30 and began supplying electricity and heat to the whole district on Oct 1. It is expected to cut CO2 emissions by about 25%
The name Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi was chosen on Apr 21, 2026. It is the fourth Midtown, after Roppongi, Hibiya and Yaesu

hojosen.title: Nihonbashi Riverwalk
hojosen.body: Nihonbashi Riverwalk is the area name that groups several redevelopments Mitsui Fudosan and others are carrying out along the Nihonbashi River. Together with moving the Nihonbashi section of the Metropolitan Expressway underground, the plan aims to create walkways and waterfront spaces along the river. Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi is its first phase.

hojosen.title: The year between completion and opening
hojosen.body: In large mixed-use buildings, tenant fit-out work (known in Japan as B-work and C-work) and hotel opening preparations continue after the building itself is completed. A gap of six months to more than a year before the grand opening is typical. Tokyo Midtown Yaesu, for example, was completed in August 2022 and opened in March 2023.

stories.title: 札幌市が中島公園隣接の新MICE施設 基本計画案を公表 事業費597億円、33年度供用へ
stories.summary: 札幌市は10月6日、南10条西3丁目に建てる新MICE施設の基本計画案を公表。延べ約3万8400㎡、事業費597億円で2033年度の供用開始を目指します。
body: 札幌市は10月6日、地下鉄南北線・中島公園駅に隣接する「（仮称）新MICE施設」の整備基本計画案を公表しました。建設地は南10条西3丁目で、建物は地下1階・地上5階建て、延べ面積は約3万8400平方メートル。概算整備事業費は税込み約597億円で、内訳は建物整備費約492億円、土地取得費約105億円です。2025年9月に示した整備方針の592億円から5億円増えました。
施設には約2000平方メートルのメインホール、約3200平方メートルの多目的ホール、15室の会議室を設け、3000〜5000人規模の学会を単館で開催できる機能を持たせます。周辺ホテルと連携すれば5000〜1万人規模にも対応する方針です。地下1階で中島公園駅と直結する計画です。
事業方式は、民間が建設して市に引き渡すBT方式と、運営権を民間に売却するコンセッション方式の組み合わせで、事業期間は15〜20年を想定。2028年度に事業者を選定し、2029年度基本設計、2031年度着工、2033年度の竣工・供用開始を目指します。北海道新聞によると、別に計上される中島公園駅の改良費を加えると実質的な事業費は600億円を超える見通しで、市議会からは注文や懸念も相次ぎました。
stories.commentary: 597億円を延べ面積で割ると、1平方メートルあたり約155万円。北海道新聞がそう計算していました。ホールや会議場は柱のない大きな空間が要るので、オフィスやマンションより単価が高くなるのは自然なんですが、それでも建設費の上がり方を実感する数字です。10月6日号でお伝えした広島のアリーナ構想は「民間が建てて市に寄付し、運営も民間」という形でした。札幌の新MICEは、民間が建てた建物を市がお金を払って買い取り、運営する権利だけを民間に売る形です。どちらも「所有は市、運営は民間」ですが、建設費を最初に誰が負担するかが違います。札幌は市が払う。だから市議会で議論になるわけです。学会や国際会議を呼ぶ施設は、稼働率が読みにくい一方で、周辺のホテルや飲食にお金が落ちる。市の試算では経済波及効果が年563億円とのことですが、建物に600億円を投じる判断を、皆さんはどう見ますか。
briefing: スケジュールは2026年度に基本計画策定、2028年度に事業者選定と土地売買契約、2029年度基本設計、2030年度実施設計、2031年度着工、2033年度竣工
中島公園駅との接続などの駅改良費（整備方針では24億円）は597億円に含まれていない
STVニュース北海道によると、市は経済波及効果を年間563億円と試算
基本計画案は市議会の委員会に報告された段階。市は2026年度中の基本計画策定を予定

hojosen.title: BT方式とコンセッション
hojosen.body: BT（Build-Transfer）は民間事業者が施設を建設し、完成後に所有権を自治体へ移す方式。コンセッションは、自治体が所有する施設の運営権を民間に売却し、民間が料金収入で運営する方式です。札幌の新MICEは両者を組み合わせ、建設は民間のノウハウを使いつつ、建物は市が持つ形をとります。

hojosen.title: 札幌のMICE計画の経緯
hojosen.body: 札幌市は2018年にも中島公園周辺で新MICE施設の基本計画をまとめていましたが、その後計画は見直され、2025年9月に改めて整備方針（事業費592億円）を公表。今回の基本計画案はそれを具体化したものです。

en.title: Sapporo unveils a ¥59.7 billion convention center plan next to Nakajima Park, opening in fiscal 2033
en.summary: On Oct 6, the City of Sapporo released a draft basic plan for a new convention center in its Minami 10-jo Nishi 3-chome area. The building would have about 38,400 m² (413,000 sq ft) of floor area and cost ¥59.7 billion, with opening targeted for fiscal 2033.
body: The City of Sapporo, the largest city on Japan's northern island of Hokkaido, released on Oct 6 a draft basic plan for its New MICE Facility (a working name), a convention center for meetings, incentive travel, conferences and exhibitions. The site, at Minami 10-jo Nishi 3-chome, is next to Nakajima-koen Station on the Namboku subway line. The building would have one basement level and five stories above ground, with a total floor area of about 38,400 m² (413,000 sq ft). The rough project cost is about ¥59.7 billion including tax, made up of about ¥49.2 billion for the building and about ¥10.5 billion for land. That is ¥500 million more than the ¥59.2 billion in the development policy the city presented in September 2025.

The facility would have a main hall of about 2,000 m² (21,500 sq ft), a multipurpose hall of about 3,200 m² (34,400 sq ft) and 15 meeting rooms, allowing it to host academic conferences of 3,000 to 5,000 people on its own. Working with nearby hotels, the city aims to handle events of 5,000 to 10,000 people. The plan calls for a direct connection to Nakajima-koen Station on the first basement level.

The project would combine a build-transfer (BT) approach, in which a private company builds the facility and hands it over to the city, with a concession, in which the city sells the right to run it to a private operator. The project period is expected to be 15 to 20 years. The city aims to select an operator in fiscal 2028 (Japan's fiscal year runs from April to March), carry out basic design in fiscal 2029, start construction in fiscal 2031, and complete and open the building in fiscal 2033. According to the Hokkaido Shimbun, adding the separately budgeted cost of improving Nakajima-koen Station would push the effective project cost above ¥60 billion, and city council members raised a series of requests and concerns.
en.commentary: Divide ¥59.7 billion by the total floor area and you get about ¥1.55 million per square meter. That's the calculation the Hokkaido Shimbun ran. Halls and conference spaces need large column-free rooms, so it's natural for the unit cost to be higher than for offices or condos. Even so, it's a number that makes you feel how much construction costs have risen. The Hiroshima arena plan we covered on Oct 6 worked like this: a private company builds it, donates it to the city, and a private company runs it. Sapporo's new convention center works differently. The city pays to buy a building that a private company builds, then sells only the right to operate it. Both end up with the city owning and the private sector operating. What's different is who pays for construction up front. In Sapporo, the city pays. That's why it's being debated in the city council. A facility built to attract academic and international conferences has hard-to-predict occupancy, but it brings money into nearby hotels and restaurants. The city estimates the economic ripple effect at ¥56.3 billion a year. How do you see the decision to put ¥60 billion into a building?
briefing: The schedule: basic plan finalized in fiscal 2026, operator selection and land purchase contract in fiscal 2028, basic design in fiscal 2029, detailed design in fiscal 2030, construction start in fiscal 2031 and completion in fiscal 2033
Station improvement costs, such as the connection to Nakajima-koen Station (¥2.4 billion in the development policy), are not included in the ¥59.7 billion
According to STV News Hokkaido, the city estimates the economic ripple effect at ¥56.3 billion a year
The draft basic plan has so far been reported to a city council committee. The city plans to finalize the basic plan within fiscal 2026

hojosen.title: BT and concessions
hojosen.body: In a BT (build-transfer) scheme, a private company builds a facility and transfers ownership to the local government once it is finished. In a concession, a local government sells the right to run a facility it owns to a private company, which operates it on fee revenue. Sapporo's new convention center combines the two, drawing on private-sector know-how for construction while the city keeps ownership of the building.

hojosen.title: How Sapporo's convention plan got here
hojosen.body: Sapporo drew up a basic plan for a new convention center around Nakajima Park back in 2018, but the plan was later reconsidered. In September 2025 the city released a fresh development policy (with a project cost of ¥59.2 billion), and the new draft basic plan fleshes it out.

stories.title: JR東日本初の3Dプリンター駅舎 釜石線・小佐野駅を建て替え、現地で直接造形は駅舎で日本初
stories.summary: JR東日本は築78年の釜石線小佐野駅（岩手県釜石市）を建設用3Dプリンターで建て替え。現場で直接造形する方式は駅舎で日本初。2027年3月利用開始予定です。
body: JR東日本は9月30日、釜石線・小佐野駅（岩手県釜石市）の駅舎を建設用3Dプリンターを活用して建て替えると発表しました。現在の駅舎は築78年で老朽化が進んでいます。新駅舎は鉄筋コンクリート造の平屋建てで、延べ床面積は約7.5平方メートル。工事は10月に着手し、2027年3月の利用開始を予定しています。日経クロステックによると、施工は3Dプリンター建築を手がける會澤高圧コンクリートが担当します。
建設用3Dプリンターによる駅舎はJR西日本の紀勢本線・初島駅（和歌山県）が2025年7月に世界で初めて供用を始めていますが、JR東日本管内では今回が初めてです。小佐野駅では建設現場に3Dプリンターを設置し、その場で直接造形する方法をとり、これは駅舎として日本初とされています。
新駅舎のデザインコンセプトは「山から海へ流れる風のみち」。駅が釜石の山間部と海辺をつなぐ位置にあることにちなんだものです。JR東日本は今回の工事を通じて、3Dプリンターによるデザイン性の向上や施工品質の安定化、省人化といった新しい施工方法の可能性を検証するとしています。
stories.commentary: 延べ床面積7.5平方メートル。畳でいえば4畳半ほどの小さな建物です。でも、僕はこの「小ささ」にこそ意味があると思っています。地方の小さな駅は、乗降客が少なくても駅舎を直さないわけにはいかない。ところが職人さんの手配や型枠の製作を考えると、小さい建物ほど1平方メートルあたりのコストは割高になりがちです。3Dプリンターは、型枠を組まずにコンクリートを層状に積み上げていくので、小さくて形の自由な建物ほど向いているんです。初島駅との違いは、部材を工場で作って運ぶのではなく、現場にプリンターを持ち込んで直接造形する点。運搬の制約から解放されるかわりに、現場の気温や湿度でコンクリートの固まり方が変わるので、品質を安定させる技術が試されます。皆さんの最寄り駅の駅舎は、築何年か知っていますか。JR東日本が検証するのは、デザイン性、品質の安定、省人化の3つ。新駅舎の利用開始は2027年3月です。
briefing: 小佐野駅は釜石線（花巻〜釜石）の駅で、現駅舎は築78年
JR西日本の初島駅は2025年7月22日に利用開始した世界初の3Dプリンター駅舎。JR東日本の小佐野駅はそれに続く国内2例目の3Dプリンター駅舎となる
JR東日本は3Dプリンターを使った駅のベンチ（災害対応型トイレ兼用）を會澤高圧コンクリートと製作した実績がある

hojosen.title: 建設用3Dプリンター
hojosen.body: セメント系の材料をノズルから押し出し、層状に積み重ねて壁などを造形する技術。型枠が不要で曲面がつくりやすく、省人化につながる一方、現行の建築基準法では構造部材として使う際の扱いが整理途上で、小規模な建物や非構造部材から実用化が進んでいます。

hojosen.title: ローカル駅舎の更新
hojosen.body: 地方路線では戦後すぐに建てられた木造・RC造の駅舎が多く残り、老朽化と利用者減少が同時に進んでいます。鉄道各社は駅舎の小型化や簡易化で維持費を抑えており、3Dプリンターはその選択肢の一つとして試されています。

en.title: JR East plans its first 3D-printed station, printed on site at Kosano Station in Iwate
en.summary: JR East will rebuild the 78-year-old Kosano Station on the Kamaishi Line in Kamaishi, Iwate Prefecture, with a construction 3D printer. Printing directly on site is a first for a station building in Japan. The new station is set to open in March 2027.
body: East Japan Railway Company (JR East) announced on Sep 30 that it will use a construction 3D printer to rebuild the station building at Kosano Station on the Kamaishi Line, in Kamaishi, a city in Iwate Prefecture in northeastern Japan. The current building is 78 years old and has deteriorated. The new one will be a single-story reinforced concrete structure with a total floor area of about 7.5 m² (81 sq ft). Work starts in October, and the station is scheduled to open in March 2027. According to Nikkei Xtech, Aizawa Koatsu Concrete, a company that builds with 3D printers, is carrying out the construction.

The world's first 3D-printed station building, Hatsushima Station on JR West's Kisei Main Line in Wakayama Prefecture, went into service in July 2025, but this is the first in JR East's territory. At Kosano Station, the printer will be set up on the construction site and the structure printed right there, which is said to be a first for a station building in Japan.

The design concept for the new station is "a path for the wind flowing from the mountains to the sea," a nod to the station's location linking Kamaishi's mountain areas with its coast. JR East says it will use the project to test what this new construction method can offer, including better design, more consistent build quality and fewer workers on site.
en.commentary: A total floor area of 7.5 m² (81 sq ft). That's about four and a half tatami mats, the size of a classic small Japanese room. But I think the smallness is exactly what makes this meaningful. At small rural stations, even if few passengers use them, the railway can't just leave the building alone. Yet once you factor in arranging skilled workers and making formwork, the smaller the building, the higher the cost per square meter tends to be. A 3D printer builds up concrete in layers without any formwork, so it suits small, freely shaped buildings best. The difference from Hatsushima Station is that the parts aren't made in a factory and shipped in. Instead, the printer is brought to the site and prints the structure in place. That frees the project from transport limits, but on site, temperature and humidity change how the concrete sets, so the technology for keeping quality consistent gets put to the test. Do you know how old the building at your nearest station is? JR East will be testing three things: design, consistent quality and labor savings. The new station opens in March 2027.
briefing: Kosano Station is on the Kamaishi Line (Hanamaki to Kamaishi), and its current building is 78 years old
JR West's Hatsushima Station, which opened on July 22, 2025, was the world's first 3D-printed station building. JR East's Kosano Station will be the second 3D-printed station building in Japan
JR East has previously worked with Aizawa Koatsu Concrete to make a 3D-printed station bench that doubles as an emergency toilet for disasters

hojosen.title: Construction 3D printers
hojosen.body: A technology that pushes cement-based material out of a nozzle and stacks it in layers to form walls and other elements. It needs no formwork, makes curves easy and reduces labor. However, under Japan's current Building Standards Act, the rules for using printed elements as structural members are still being worked out, so practical use is spreading first in small buildings and non-structural elements.

hojosen.title: Renewing rural stations
hojosen.body: Many wooden and reinforced concrete station buildings put up shortly after World War II remain on rural lines, and they are aging just as ridership is falling. Railway companies are keeping maintenance costs down by making station buildings smaller and simpler, and 3D printing is being tried as one of those options.

stories.title: 改正建築士法の施行日が2027年4月1日に決定 設計・監理契約は面積を問わず書面が義務に
stories.summary: 国交省は10月6日、改正建築士法の契約部分を2027年4月1日に施行する政令の閣議決定を発表。面積を問わず全ての設計・工事監理契約が書面義務の対象になります。
body: 国土交通省は10月6日、建築士法の一部を改正する法律（令和8年法律第74号）の施行に伴う関係政令が閣議決定されたと発表しました。BuildApp Newsによると、閣議決定された政令は2本で、1本は改正法のうち契約に関する規定を2027年4月1日から施行すると定めるもの、もう1本は建築士法施行令を改める運用上の整備です。施行されるのは、建築士事務所が行う全ての設計・工事監理の受託契約の書面化と、報酬の算定根拠を示す見積書を作成する努力義務です。
現行制度では、書面による契約の相互交付が義務づけられているのは延べ面積300平方メートル超の新築などに限られ、それ以下は「望ましい」とされてきました。改正法は7月24日に参院で可決・成立し、7月31日に公布されています。契約・見積書に関する部分は公布から1年以内、在学中の建築士試験受験など資格要件の部分は3年以内に政令で定める日から施行する建て付けで、今回は前者の日付が決まった形です。
受験要件の緩和や二級・木造建築士の実務経験短縮など、資格制度の施行日は今回の政令には含まれておらず、別途定められる見通しです。施行まで約半年。小規模な住宅やリフォームの設計を受ける事務所も、契約書と見積書の運用を見直す期間に入ります。
stories.commentary: 書面契約の全面義務化は、僕たち建築士事務所の仕事のやり方そのものに関わる話です。300平方メートル以下の住宅や店舗では、いまも口頭と図面だけで設計が始まるケースが珍しくありません。設計料がいくらで、どこまでの業務を含むのかが曖昧なまま進み、最後にもめる。これを法律で止めに来たのが今回の改正です。見積書の作成は努力義務にとどまりますが、「報酬の算定根拠を示す」という考え方が条文に入った意味は小さくないと思います。僕自身、小さな店舗の内装改修でも概算見積に項目ごとの内訳と根拠を付けて出すようにしていますが、根拠を書くと自分の業務範囲も自然と整理されます。皆さんの事務所では、設計契約を書面にするまでにどれくらいの手間がかかっていますか。施行は2027年4月1日。契約書と見積書の雛形を整える時間は、あと半年です。
briefing: 10月6日、改正建築士法（令和8年法律第74号）の施行に伴う関係政令を閣議決定
契約に関する規定の施行日は2027年4月1日。全ての設計・工事監理契約が書面義務の対象に
見積書の作成は努力義務。受験資格など資格制度の施行日は別途政令で定める見通し

hojosen.title: 書面契約の義務（現行）
hojosen.body: 2015年施行の改正建築士法で、延べ面積300平方メートル超の建築物の新築などに関する設計・工事監理契約は、必要事項を記した書面を当事者が相互に交付することが義務づけられました。300平方メートル以下は法律上の義務がなく、書面による契約が「望まれる」扱いでした。

hojosen.title: 今回の改正法の二段階施行
hojosen.body: 令和8年の改正建築士法は、契約・見積書に関する部分を公布から1年以内、在学中受験の解禁など資格要件に関する部分を公布から3年以内に、それぞれ政令で定める日から施行する構成です。公布は2026年7月31日でした。

en.title: Japan sets April 1, 2027 for written contracts on all architectural design work, whatever the size
en.summary: Japan's construction ministry announced on Oct 6 that the cabinet approved an ordinance putting the contract provisions of the revised Kenchikushi Act into force on April 1, 2027. From then on, every design and construction supervision contract must be in writing, regardless of floor area.
body: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) announced on Oct 6 that the cabinet had approved the government ordinances needed to bring into force the Act Partially Amending the Kenchikushi Act (Act No. 74 of 2026). The Kenchikushi Act is the law that licenses architects in Japan and regulates their offices. According to BuildApp News, the cabinet approved two ordinances. One puts the revised law's provisions on contracts into force on April 1, 2027, and the other makes operational updates to the Act's enforcement order. The provisions taking effect require architect offices to put every contract for design and construction supervision (the architect's job of checking that construction matches the drawings) in writing, and add a best-effort obligation to prepare estimates that show how fees are calculated.

Under the current system, the mutual exchange of written contracts is mandatory only for projects such as new buildings with a total floor area of more than 300 m² (3,200 sq ft). Below that, written contracts have merely been described as desirable. The revised law passed the House of Councillors, the upper house of Japan's parliament, on July 24 and was promulgated on July 31. It was structured so that the parts on contracts and estimates take effect on a date set by ordinance within one year of promulgation, and the parts on license requirements, such as allowing students to take the kenchikushi exam while still in school, within three years. This ordinance sets the date for the former.

The ordinances do not cover the start dates for the licensing changes, such as relaxed exam eligibility and shorter practical experience requirements for second-class and wooden-building (mokuzo) kenchikushi, which are expected to be set separately. With about half a year until the rules take effect, offices that design small houses and renovations are entering a period of reviewing how they handle contracts and estimates.
en.commentary: Making written contracts mandatory across the board touches the very way we run architect offices. For houses and shops of 300 m² (3,200 sq ft) or less, it's still not unusual for a design job to start with nothing more than a conversation and some drawings. The design fee and the scope of work stay vague, and it all ends in a dispute. This revision is the law stepping in to stop that. Preparing an estimate is only a best-effort obligation, but I don't think it's a small thing that the idea of showing how a fee is calculated is now written into the law. Even for small shop interior renovations, I attach an itemized breakdown with the reasoning behind each item to my rough estimates. When you write down the reasoning, your own scope of work naturally gets sorted out too. At your office, how much effort does it take to get a design contract down in writing? The rules take effect on April 1, 2027. You have half a year to get your contract and estimate templates in order.
briefing: On Oct 6 the cabinet approved the government ordinances for bringing the revised Kenchikushi Act (Act No. 74 of 2026) into force
The contract provisions take effect on April 1, 2027. Every design and construction supervision contract will have to be in writing
Preparing estimates is a best-effort obligation. Start dates for the licensing changes, such as exam eligibility, are expected to be set by a separate ordinance

hojosen.title: Written contracts under current rules
hojosen.body: The revised Kenchikushi Act that took effect in 2015 required the parties to design and construction supervision contracts for projects such as new buildings with a total floor area of more than 300 m² (3,200 sq ft) to exchange written documents setting out the required terms. For 300 m² (3,200 sq ft) or less there was no legal obligation, and written contracts were only encouraged.

hojosen.title: A revision in two stages
hojosen.body: The 2026 revision of the Kenchikushi Act takes effect in two parts, each on a date set by ordinance. The parts on contracts and estimates come within one year of promulgation, and the parts on license requirements, such as opening the exam to students still in school, within three years. The law was promulgated on July 31, 2026.

stories.title: 中野サンプラザ再整備計画の改定が3カ月延期 2027年5月へ、34年度完成目標は維持
stories.summary: 中野区は白紙になった中野サンプラザ再開発の方針となる再整備事業計画の改定を2027年2月から5月に延期。有識者会議などの意見を受け、検討に時間が要るとしました。
body: 東京都中野区は10月5日、事業費の高騰で再開発計画が白紙になった「中野サンプラザ」について、再開発の方針となる「再整備事業計画」の改定時期を2027年2月から同年5月に3カ月遅らせると発表しました。朝日新聞によると、9月18日に初会合を開いた有識者会議や区議会からの意見を受け、検討に時間が必要と判断したものです。10月6日の区議会建設委員会でも区が同じ方針を説明しました。
区は8月に改定に向けた骨子をまとめ、新施設に入る住宅は1100戸程度を上限の目安とすること、ホールは3000人規模を基本とすること、一部敷地に定期借地権を活用することなどを示していました。当初の流れでは10月に素案、2027年2月に改定という予定でした。
区は建て替えについて2030年度着工、2034年度完成を目指しています。朝日新聞によると、区幹部は「数カ月の遅れなので工期自体にそこまでの影響はないはず」としていますが、東京新聞は、2034年度完成目標への影響について区が明言していないと伝えています。
stories.commentary: 中野サンプラザの再開発は、建設費の高騰で2025年に計画が白紙になった象徴的な案件です。今回の3カ月延期そのものは小さな話ですが、僕が注目しているのは骨子に入った「定期借地権」と「ホール3000人規模」の2点です。土地を売って建物を建てる方式ではなく、区が土地を貸して地代を受け取る。事業者から見れば初期の土地代が要らない分、工事費の高騰に耐えやすくなります。一方でホールは、以前検討されていた最大5000人から3000人規模が基本になりました。建設費が上がると、まず削られるのは収益を生みにくい公共的な部分です。計画を練り直すというのは、何を残して何を小さくするかを決め直す作業でもあります。皆さんは、中野の新しい顔に何が残ってほしいですか。2034年度の完成目標に向けて、2027年5月の改定計画が次の節目になります。
briefing: 中野区が10月5日、再整備事業計画の改定を2027年2月から5月に3カ月延期すると発表
8月の骨子は住宅1100戸程度を上限の目安、ホール3000人規模を基本、定期借地権の活用を明記
2030年度着工・2034年度完成の目標は維持。工期への影響は区幹部が「限定的」との見方

hojosen.title: 計画白紙までの経緯
hojosen.body: 中野サンプラザは2023年に閉館。野村不動産などによる再開発は建設費の高騰で事業費が大きく膨らみ、2024年に認可申請が取り下げられ、2025年に計画が白紙となりました。区は2026年3月、既存建物の改修・再利用を否定し、2030年度着工・2034年度完成という新しい目標を示しています。

hojosen.title: 定期借地権
hojosen.body: 土地の所有者が期間を定めて土地を貸し、借り手がその上に建物を建てる仕組み。区が土地を売らずに地代収入を得る一方、事業者は土地取得費を抑えられます。期間満了後の建物の扱いは契約で定めます。

en.title: Tokyo's Nakano Ward delays the Nakano Sun Plaza rebuilding plan by three months to May 2027
en.summary: Nakano Ward has pushed back the revision of its redevelopment plan for Nakano Sun Plaza, whose earlier scheme was scrapped, from February to May 2027. The ward said it needs more time after hearing from an expert panel and others.
body: Tokyo's Nakano Ward announced on Oct 5 that it will delay by three months, from February to May 2027, the revision of its redevelopment project plan for Nakano Sun Plaza, the landmark concert hall complex next to Nakano Station. The plan sets the direction for the site's redevelopment, after the earlier scheme was scrapped because of soaring project costs. According to the Asahi Shimbun, the ward decided it needed more time to deliberate after hearing from an expert panel that first met on Sep 18 and from the ward assembly. The ward gave the same explanation at the ward assembly's construction committee on Oct 6.

In August the ward put together an outline for the revision. It set about 1,100 homes as a rough upper limit for housing in the new complex, took a hall for about 3,000 people as the baseline, and proposed using a fixed-term land lease on part of the site. Under the original timeline, a draft was due in October and the revision in February 2027.

The ward is aiming to start construction in fiscal 2030 and finish in fiscal 2034 (Japan's fiscal year runs from April to March). According to the Asahi Shimbun, a senior ward official said, "It's a delay of a few months, so it shouldn't have much effect on the construction schedule itself." The Tokyo Shimbun, however, reported that the ward has not said clearly whether the fiscal 2034 completion target will be affected.
en.commentary: The Nakano Sun Plaza redevelopment became a symbol of rising construction costs when its plan was scrapped in 2025. The three-month delay itself is a small thing. What I'm watching are two points in the outline: the fixed-term land lease and the hall for about 3,000 people. Instead of selling the land and building on it, the ward leases the land and collects ground rent. For a developer, not having to pay for the land up front makes it easier to absorb rising construction costs. The hall, meanwhile, has gone from a maximum of 5,000 people in earlier studies to a baseline of about 3,000. When construction costs go up, the first things to get cut are the public parts that don't make much money. Reworking a plan also means deciding all over again what to keep and what to shrink. What would you want to survive in the new face of Nakano? On the way to the fiscal 2034 completion target, the revised plan in May 2027 is the next milestone.
briefing: On Oct 5, Nakano Ward announced a three-month delay in revising the redevelopment project plan, from February to May 2027
The August outline set about 1,100 homes as a rough upper limit for housing, took a hall for about 3,000 people as the baseline and called for using a fixed-term land lease
The targets of starting construction in fiscal 2030 and finishing in fiscal 2034 remain. A senior ward official expects only a limited impact on the construction schedule

hojosen.title: How the plan was scrapped
hojosen.body: Nakano Sun Plaza closed in 2023. The redevelopment led by Nomura Real Estate Development and others saw its project cost balloon as construction costs soared, the application for approval was withdrawn in 2024, and the plan was scrapped in 2025. In March 2026 the ward ruled out renovating and reusing the existing building and set new targets of starting construction in fiscal 2030 and finishing in fiscal 2034.

hojosen.title: Fixed-term land leases
hojosen.body: A system in which a landowner leases land for a set period and the tenant builds on it. The ward earns ground rent without selling the land, while the developer keeps land acquisition costs down. What happens to the building when the lease ends is set out in the contract.

stories.title: 神戸・三宮のサンセンタープラザ3棟建て替え コーディネーターにRIA選定 権利者約400人
stories.summary: 三宮の商業ビル3棟の区分所有者らでつくる再開発協議会が、建て替え検討を支援するコーディネート業務の委託先にアール・アイ・エーを選定。事業手法や時期は未定です。
body: 神戸・三宮センター街の「さんプラザ」「センタープラザ」「センタープラザ西館」の3棟の建て替えに向け、区分所有者らでつくる「サンセンタープラザ地区再開発協議会」が、公募していた再開発コーディネート業務の委託先にアール・アイ・エー（RIA）を選定しました。日刊建設工業新聞と建設通信新聞が10月6日に報じました。業務は建て替え整備に向けた検討と協議会の運営支援で、委託期間は2027年3月31日まで。再開発準備組合の設立に向けた合意形成の支援も担います。
3棟はさんプラザが1970年、センタープラザが1975年、センタープラザ西館が1978年の竣工で、いずれも築半世紀前後。神戸新聞によると区分所有者は約400人で、神戸市も区分所有者の一人として協議会に加わっています。協議会は2026年7月24日に発足し、2021年の「あり方検討会」、2024年の「建て替え研究会」を経て、建て替えの実現可能性を具体的に検討する段階に入りました。
再開発の事業手法やスケジュールは未定で、協議会は数年かけて基本計画案をまとめる見通しです。建て替えが正式に決まったわけではなく、まずは事業の枠組みと既存の権利の扱いを固めることが当面の目的になります。
stories.commentary: 三宮センター街の3棟は、神戸の人なら誰でも知っている商業ビルです。難しいのは、建物の古さではなく権利の数。区分所有者が約400人いて、しかもその一人が神戸市という構図です。マンションの建て替えなら住戸の数だけ合意が要りますが、商業ビルの場合は店の売上や立地の価値が一区画ごとに違うので、同じ面積でも「等価」の考え方が揃いません。コーディネーターの役割は、設計を描くことより先に、この400の事情を一つの事業の枠に収める道筋を作ることです。2026年4月に施行された改正区分所有法では、所在不明の区分所有者を決議の分母から外す仕組みが入りましたが、合意形成の本体はやはり人の話し合いです。皆さんの街にも、半世紀前の区分所有ビルはありませんか。今回の委託期間は2027年3月末まで。その時点で事業手法の骨格がどこまで見えているか、まずそこを見ておくといいと思います。
briefing: 三宮の商業ビル3棟の再開発協議会がコーディネート業務の委託先にアール・アイ・エーを選定
3棟は1970〜78年竣工、区分所有者は約400人。神戸市も区分所有者として参加
委託期間は2027年3月末まで。事業手法・スケジュールは未定で、建て替えは正式決定前

hojosen.title: 再開発コーディネーター
hojosen.body: 市街地再開発の初期段階で、権利者の意向把握、事業手法の検討、準備組合の設立支援などを担うコンサルタント。設計者や施工者とは役割が異なり、合意形成と事業の枠組みづくりが主な仕事です。RIAは再開発計画を数多く手がける設計・コンサルタント会社です。

hojosen.title: 改正区分所有法（2026年4月施行）
hojosen.body: 所在不明の区分所有者を裁判所の決定を経て決議の分母から除外できる制度が新設されたほか、耐震性不足など一定の事由があるマンション等では建て替え決議の要件が緩和されました。商業ビルも区分所有建物であれば同法の対象です。

en.title: About 400 owners of three aging buildings in Kobe's Sannomiya pick RIA to coordinate a rebuild
en.summary: A redevelopment council formed by the unit owners of three commercial buildings in Sannomiya, central Kobe, has chosen RIA to provide coordination services as it studies rebuilding. The method and timing are still undecided.
body: The Sun Center Plaza District Redevelopment Council, made up of the unit owners of three buildings on Sannomiya Center Gai, a covered shopping street in Sannomiya, the main downtown of the port city of Kobe, has chosen RIA for the redevelopment coordination contract it had put out to public tender. The buildings are San Plaza, Center Plaza and Center Plaza West, and the goal is to rebuild them. The construction trade papers Nikkan Kensetsu Kogyo Shimbun and Kensetsu Tsushin Shimbun reported the selection on Oct 6. The work covers studies toward rebuilding and support for running the council, and the contract runs until March 31, 2027. RIA will also help build consensus toward setting up a redevelopment preparatory association.

San Plaza was completed in 1970, Center Plaza in 1975 and Center Plaza West in 1978, so all three are around half a century old. According to the Kobe Shimbun, there are about 400 unit owners, people who each own a section of a building much like condominium owners, and the City of Kobe is also one of them and sits on the council. The council was launched on July 24, 2026, following a study group on the buildings' future in 2021 and a rebuilding research group in 2024, and has now reached the stage of looking concretely at whether a rebuild is feasible.

The redevelopment method and schedule have not been decided, and the council is expected to spend several years putting together a draft basic plan. Rebuilding has not been formally decided. For now, the main goal is to settle the project framework and how existing property rights will be handled.
en.commentary: Anyone from Kobe knows these three commercial buildings on Sannomiya Center Gai. The hard part isn't how old they are. It's how many rights are involved. There are about 400 unit owners, and one of them is the City of Kobe. When a condominium is rebuilt, you need agreement from as many owners as there are units. But in a commercial building, each section's sales and location value are different, so even two spaces of the same size don't line up on what counts as equal. A coordinator's job, before drawing any design, is to map out a way to fit those 400 different situations into a single project. The revised Act on Building Unit Ownership, which took effect in April 2026, added a way to remove owners who can't be located from the count used for votes. Still, the real work of reaching consensus is people talking to each other. Is there a half-century-old building with many owners in your town too? This contract runs until the end of March 2027. I think the first thing to watch is how much of the project's framework is visible by then.
briefing: The redevelopment council for three commercial buildings in Sannomiya selected RIA for its coordination contract
The three buildings were completed between 1970 and 1978 and have about 400 unit owners. The City of Kobe takes part as one of the owners
The contract runs until the end of March 2027. The project method and schedule are undecided, and rebuilding has not yet been formally decided

hojosen.title: Redevelopment coordinators
hojosen.body: A consultant who, in the early stages of an urban redevelopment, gauges what the property owners want, studies how the project could be carried out, and helps set up a preparatory association. The role is different from the architect's or the builder's: the main work is building consensus and shaping the project framework. RIA is a design and consulting firm that has worked on many redevelopment plans.

hojosen.title: The revised Unit Ownership Act (April 2026)
hojosen.body: The revision created a system that lets owners who cannot be located be removed, with a court's approval, from the count used for votes. It also eased the requirements for votes to rebuild condominiums and similar buildings in certain cases, such as insufficient earthquake resistance. Commercial buildings are also covered by the law if they are divided into separately owned units.

stories.title: 国交省が「標準労務費」の行き渡りを調べる実態調査へ 鉄筋・型枠の見積もりと左官・内装の賃金
stories.summary: 国土交通省は10月5日、改正建設業法の「労務費の基準」が現場で守られているかを調べる新たな実態調査の方針を決定。見積もりと賃金の両面で基準値と比べます。
body: 国土交通省は10月5日、中央建設業審議会の「労務費の基準に関するワーキンググループ」第13回会合を開き、改正建設業法で定めた「労務費に関する基準（標準労務費）」が現場でどう運用されているかを把握する調査の実施方針を決めました。議題は基準の実効性確保策の状況、既存調査のフォローアップ、新規調査の実施の3点です。
日刊建設工業新聞によると、新たな調査は民間建築分野の実態把握が狙いで、見積もり段階の調査は鉄筋と型枠の2職種、賃金の支払い段階の調査は左官と内装の2職種を対象にします。見積書に記載された労務費を、工種・作業別に設定された標準労務費の基準値と比較し、著しく低い見積もりや賃金への不行き渡りがないかを個々の請負構造に分け入って確かめます。
労務費の基準は2025年12月に中央建設業審議会が作成し、公共・民間の発注者と建設業団体に実施を勧告したものです。基準値は職種・都道府県ごとに、1トン当たりや1平方メートル当たりといった単位施工量当たりの労務費で示されます。9月30日号でお伝えした井林国交相と建設4団体の意見交換でも、技能者の賃上げの継続が最大の議題でした。
stories.commentary: 標準労務費というのは、簡単に言えば「この作業なら職人さんの手間賃はこれくらい」という国の目安です。鉄筋なら1トン組むのにいくら、型枠なら1平方メートルでいくら。2025年12月にこの基準ができて、著しく低い見積もりは法律違反になりました。ただ、基準があることと、お金が職人さんの手元まで届くことは別なんです。建設の現場は、元請け、1次下請け、2次下請けと階段のようにお金が流れていきます。途中のどこかで削られると、一番下で手を動かす人の賃金だけが上がらない。今回の調査が面白いのは、「見積もり」と「支払い」の両方を見ることです。見積書に書いた労務費と、実際に左官や内装の職人さんに払われた賃金を、別々の職種で追いかける。皆さんが家を建てるときの見積書にも、本当は同じ構造が隠れています。基準値を下回る見積もりは、安い買い物ではなく、誰かの賃金を削った結果かもしれない。調査の対象は鉄筋、型枠、左官、内装の4職種です。
briefing: ワーキンググループは2024年9月に設置され、2025年10月の第11回で基準案をとりまとめ。12月2日の中央建設業審議会で「労務費に関する基準」を作成し実施を勧告した（国交省）
基準値の初弾は14職種で、改正建設業法は2025年12月に全面施行。基準を著しく下回る見積もりや、発注者による不当な値下げ要求が禁止された（建通新聞・日刊建設工業新聞）
日経クロステックによると国交省は標準労務費の運用状況の調査を拡充する方針で、公共工事より把握が難しい民間建築の請負構造が焦点になる
