hojosen.title: 重層下請けと賃金
hojosen.body: 日本の建設現場は元請けの下に複数の下請け層が連なる重層構造で、工事費が各層で管理費として差し引かれるため、最下層の技能者の賃金が上がりにくい構造があります。公共工事の設計労務単価は14年連続で引き上げられていますが、民間工事では単価の反映が追いつかないことが課題とされてきました。

hojosen.title: 改正建設業法の3本柱
hojosen.body: 2024年に成立した改正建設業法は、労務費の適正化、資材高騰の価格転嫁、工期ダンピングの禁止を柱としています。労務費の基準はこのうち処遇改善の中核で、基準を守らない見積もりには国交省や都道府県が勧告や指導を行える仕組みです。

en.title: Japan to survey whether its new standard labor costs are reaching construction workers
en.summary: On Oct 5, Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) decided on a new survey of whether the labor cost standard set under the amended Construction Business Act is being followed on site. It will compare both estimates and actual wages against the standard values.
body: Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) decided on Oct 5 how it will survey the way the labor cost standard, known as standard labor costs, is working in practice on construction sites. The standard was set under the amended Construction Business Act, the law that governs construction contractors in Japan. The decision came at the 13th meeting of the Working Group on the Labor Cost Standard under the Central Construction Industry Council, an advisory body to the ministry. The agenda had three items: the status of measures to make the standard effective, follow-up on existing surveys, and a new survey.

According to the Nikkan Kensetsu Kogyo Shimbun, a construction industry daily, the new survey aims to understand what is happening in private-sector building work. At the estimate stage it will look at two trades, rebar and formwork; at the wage-payment stage it will look at two others, plastering and interior finishing. Labor costs written into estimates will be compared with the standard values set for each type of work and task, and the survey will dig into individual contracting chains to check for extremely low estimates and for wages that are not reaching workers.

The standard was drawn up in December 2025 by the Central Construction Industry Council, which recommended that public and private clients and construction industry groups put it into practice. The values are set for each trade and each prefecture as a labor cost per unit of work, such as per ton or per square meter. When MLIT Minister Ibayashi met with four construction industry groups, as we reported on Sept 30, continued wage increases for skilled workers were also the top item on the agenda.
en.commentary: Standard labor costs are, put simply, the government's benchmark for how much a craftsperson's labor should cost for a given job. For rebar, it's this much to place one ton; for formwork, this much per square meter. The standard came in December 2025, and extremely low estimates became illegal. But having a standard is one thing. Getting the money all the way into the workers' hands is another. On a Japanese construction site, money flows down like a staircase: from the general contractor to the first-tier subcontractor, then to the second tier. If it gets shaved off somewhere along the way, the only people whose wages don't go up are the ones at the bottom actually doing the work. What makes this survey interesting is that it looks at both the estimate and the payment. It follows the labor costs written into estimates, and the wages actually paid to plasterers and interior finishers, using different trades for each. The estimate you get when you build a house has the same structure hidden inside it. An estimate below the standard may not be a bargain. It may be the result of cutting someone's wages. The survey covers four trades: rebar, formwork, plastering and interior finishing.
briefing: The working group was set up in September 2024 and compiled a draft standard at its 11th meeting in October 2025. On Dec 2, the Central Construction Industry Council adopted the Standard for Labor Costs and recommended its implementation (MLIT)

The first batch of standard values covers 14 trades, and the amended Construction Business Act took full effect in December 2025. Estimates far below the standard and unjust demands from clients to cut prices were banned (Kentsu Shimbun, Nikkan Kensetsu Kogyo Shimbun)

According to Nikkei xTECH, MLIT plans to expand its surveys of how standard labor costs are being applied, with the focus on contracting chains in private-sector building work, which are harder to track than public works

hojosen.title: Layers of subcontractors and wages
hojosen.body: Japanese construction sites run on a multi-tier structure, with several layers of subcontractors under the general contractor. Each layer takes a share of the construction cost as overhead, which makes it hard for wages at the bottom tier to rise. The design labor unit prices used for public works have been raised for 14 straight years, but private-sector projects have been slow to reflect them.

hojosen.title: Three pillars of the amended law
hojosen.body: The amended Construction Business Act, passed in 2024, rests on three pillars: fair labor costs, passing rising material prices on to clients, and banning unreasonably short construction schedules. The labor cost standard is the core of the effort to improve workers' pay and conditions, and MLIT or prefectural governments can issue recommendations or guidance over estimates that fail to meet it.

stories.title: 高輪ゲートウェイシティ品川側の5・6街区で「高輪築堤」を土中保存 JR東日本が建物計画変更
stories.summary: JR東日本が高輪ゲートウェイシティの第2期開発となる5・6街区で、日本初の鉄道の遺構「高輪築堤」2か所計約160mを土中保存し、建物計画を変えると発表。
body: JR東日本は10月2日、高輪ゲートウェイシティの1〜4街区に続いて開発を進める品川駅寄りの5・6街区について、高輪築堤の一部を現状のまま土中保存することを基本方針とし、可能な限り計画を変更すると発表しました。対象は信号機跡を含む5・6街区間の約50メートルと、6街区南部の約110メートルの2か所です。
Impress Watchによると、すでに決めていた区画道路の変更に加えて建物計画も見直し、6街区南部では一部の施設計画を変えて築堤への支障を避けます。高輪築堤は1872年に新橋〜横浜間で開業した日本初の鉄道が海の上を走るために築かれた石積みの堤防で、2019年からの開発工事で出土し、交通の近代化と当時の土木技術を伝える遺跡として評価されています。
1〜4街区では、第7橋梁部を含む約80メートルと公園隣接部の約40メートルが2021年に国史跡「旧新橋停車場跡及び高輪築堤跡」に追加指定され、現地保存のうえ2027年度の公開を予定しています。信号機土台部は街区内に移築保存する計画です。今回の5・6街区の判断は、その続きにあたります。
stories.commentary: 高輪ゲートウェイシティは、noteにも書いたんですが、JRが約6000億円をかけて160メートル級のビルを4棟並べた街です。その足元の地面の下に、150年前の石積みが眠っている。今回は、品川寄りの次の街区で、その石積みの上に建物を載せない判断をしました。ここで押さえておきたいのは「土中保存」という言葉です。掘り出して見せるのではなく、埋めたまま残す。見た目は何もない地面ですが、建物の基礎や地下の杭が石積みを傷めないよう、計画そのものを変える必要があります。開発する側からすると、地面の下に建てられない帯が2本走る状態です。2019年に築堤が見つかったとき、保存か開発かで大きな議論になりました。あれから7年、少なくとも5・6街区では「可能な限り変える」とJRが言った。皆さんはどう思いますか。石積みを埋めたまま残すことに、6000億円の街はどこまで付き合うべきなんでしょうね。
briefing: 5・6街区は1〜4街区の南側、品川駅寄りの第2期開発区域。JR東日本は10月2日に「TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY（5・6街区）における高輪築堤の保存方針」を公表した（JR東日本）
保存対象は「信号機跡を含む5・6街区間の約50m」と「6街区南部の約110m」。区画道路の変更に加え、建物計画を現時点で可能な限り変更する（Impress Watch・毎日新聞）
1〜4街区の高輪築堤跡は2027年度に現地公開予定で、展示空間や回廊のデザインには内藤廣氏と隈研吾氏が参加している（日経クロステック）

hojosen.title: 現地保存・移築・土中保存
hojosen.body: 遺構の保存には、掘り出したまま残して公開する現地保存、別の場所へ移す移築保存、埋め戻して将来の調査に委ねる土中保存があります。土中保存は費用と開発への影響が小さい一方、公開はできません。高輪築堤では3つの手法が街区ごとに使い分けられています。

hojosen.title: 開発と埋蔵文化財
hojosen.body: 文化財保護法では、開発中に遺跡が見つかると発掘調査と記録保存が原則で、現地保存は事業者との協議次第です。高輪築堤は2020年の出土後に学会などが保存を求め、JR東日本が一部の現地保存を決めた経緯があり、民間開発地での大規模な保存例として注目されています。

en.title: Tokyo's Takanawa Gateway City to keep 1872 railway embankment buried, changing building plans
en.summary: JR East says it will preserve two sections of the Takanawa Embankment, the remains of Japan's first railway, totaling about 160 m (525 ft), underground in Blocks 5 and 6, the second phase of Takanawa Gateway City in Tokyo, and will change its building plans to do so.
body: East Japan Railway Company (JR East) announced on Oct 2 that in Blocks 5 and 6 of Takanawa Gateway City, the next phase after Blocks 1 to 4, its basic policy will be to preserve part of the Takanawa Embankment underground as it is, changing its plans as far as possible. Takanawa Gateway City is the new district next to Takanawa Gateway Station on Tokyo's Yamanote Line, and Blocks 5 and 6 sit on the side closer to Shinagawa Station, a major rail hub in southern Tokyo. Two sections are covered: about 50 m (160 ft) between Blocks 5 and 6, including the remains of a signal, and about 110 m (360 ft) in the southern part of Block 6.

According to Impress Watch, on top of a change to a block road that had already been decided, JR East is also revising its building plans; in the southern part of Block 6, part of the facility plan will be changed to avoid affecting the embankment. The Takanawa Embankment is a stone-faced embankment built so that Japan's first railway, which opened between Shimbashi and Yokohama in 1872, could run over the sea. It was unearthed during the development work that began in 2019 and is valued as a site that shows the modernization of transport and the civil engineering of the time.

In Blocks 1 to 4, a section of about 80 m (260 ft) including the No. 7 bridge section and a section of about 40 m (130 ft) next to a park were added in 2021 to the national historic site “Former Shimbashi Station Site and Takanawa Embankment Site.” They are being preserved in place, with a public opening planned for fiscal 2027 (Japan's fiscal year starts in April). The signal base section is to be moved and preserved elsewhere within the blocks. The decision for Blocks 5 and 6 continues that work.
en.commentary: Takanawa Gateway City, as I also wrote on note, the Japanese blogging platform, is a district where JR East spent about ¥600 billion to line up four towers of around 160 m (525 ft). Under the ground at their feet, stonework from 150 years ago lies sleeping. This time, in the next blocks toward Shinagawa, JR East decided not to put buildings on top of those stones. The phrase to hold on to here is “preserved underground.” Instead of digging the stones out to show them, you leave them buried. On the surface it looks like empty ground, but the plans themselves have to change so that building foundations and underground piles don't damage the stonework. From the developer's point of view, it's like having two strips running under the site where nothing can be built. When the embankment was found in 2019, there was a big debate over preservation versus development. Seven years on, JR East has said that at least in Blocks 5 and 6 it will change things “as far as possible.” What do you think? How far should a ¥600 billion district go to accommodate stones that stay buried?
briefing: Blocks 5 and 6 are the second-phase area south of Blocks 1 to 4, toward Shinagawa Station. On Oct 2, JR East published its preservation policy for the Takanawa Embankment in TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY (Blocks 5 and 6) (JR East)

The sections to be preserved are about 50 m (160 ft) between Blocks 5 and 6, including the signal remains, and about 110 m (360 ft) in the southern part of Block 6. Besides changing the block road, JR East will change its building plans as far as currently possible (Impress Watch, Mainichi Shimbun)

The embankment remains in Blocks 1 to 4 are due to open to the public on site in fiscal 2027, and architects Hiroshi Naito and Kengo Kuma are taking part in designing the exhibition space and corridor (Nikkei xTECH)

hojosen.title: Three ways to preserve remains
hojosen.body: Archaeological remains can be preserved in place, left exposed and opened to the public; relocated to another spot; or reburied and left for future study, known as underground preservation. Underground preservation costs less and has less impact on development, but the remains cannot be shown. At the Takanawa Embankment, all three methods are being used, block by block.

hojosen.title: Development and buried heritage
hojosen.body: Under Japan's Act on Protection of Cultural Properties, when remains are found during development, the rule is to excavate and document them, while preserving them in place depends on talks with the developer. After the Takanawa Embankment was unearthed in 2020, academic societies and others called for its preservation, and JR East decided to preserve part of it in place. It has drawn attention as a large-scale preservation on privately developed land.

stories.title: ビルバオ美術館にフォスター設計の増築「アグラビタス」 既存棟の上に55mの展示棟を浮かせる
stories.summary: スペインのビルバオ美術館が10月6日、フォスター・アンド・パートナーズ設計の増築を経て再開館。V字柱で既存棟の上に55mの展示棟を浮かせました。
body: スペイン北部ビルバオの美術館「ビルバオ美術館」が10月6日、4年の工事を経て再開館しました。設計はフォスター・アンド・パートナーズと地元の建築家ルイス・マリア・ウリアルテ。増築部は「アグラビタス（重力なし）」と名付けられ、Dezeenによると長さ55メートルの橋のような展示棟が、大きなV字形の柱に支えられて既存の建物群の上にまたがり、既存の躯体には触れていません。
ArchDailyによると、新しい鉄骨構造によって既存建物の床面積は60%増え、2層で2300平方メートルの可変的な展示空間と、教育プログラムやワークショップ、事務の空間が加わりました。持ち上げた分だけ地上階が空き、約1000平方メートルの「アリアガ・アトリウム」が生まれています。鉄骨はビルバオの産業の歴史にちなんで地元産の鋼材を使いました。
The Art Newspaperは事業費を4500万ユーロと報じています。再開館後の1週間は入場無料で、1945年に建った赤れんがの旧館の正面入口も修復して復活しました。ビルバオといえばゲーリーのグッゲンハイム美術館が知られますが、こちらは1908年創設の歴史ある美術館で、スペインの古典絵画からバスクの近現代美術まで収蔵しています。
stories.commentary: 既存の美術館の上に、55メートルの箱を浮かせる。増築のやり方として、かなり思い切っています。普通、古い建物の隣や裏に足すものじゃないですか。でもビルバオ美術館は、街の中心の公園に面していて、横に広げる土地がなかった。そこでフォスターは上に積む道を選び、しかも既存の建物には荷重をかけませんでした。V字の柱を既存棟の脇に立てて、その上に鉄骨の橋を渡す。だから増築部は「浮いている」ように見えるし、工事中も旧館を壊さずに済みます。僕が面白いと思うのは、この構造の選択がそのまま建築の見え方になっていることです。重さを既存に預けない、という構造の判断が、「重力なし」という名前になった。そして持ち上げた分の地面が、1000平方メートルのアトリウムとして市民に返ってきています。日本でも増築や建て替えに悩む美術館や庁舎は多いですよね。今度古い公共建築の増築部を見かけたら、新しい部分がどこで重さを受けているか、柱の位置を探してみてください。
briefing: 設計はフォスター・アンド・パートナーズとルイス・マリア・ウリアルテ。2022年11月に起工し、約4年の工事を経て2026年10月5日に式典、6日に一般公開。10月13日まで入場無料（Dezeen・現地報道）
増築部はビルバオ産の鉄骨を用いた橋状の構造で、既存躯体に触れずにV字柱で支持。展示面積は2層で2300平方メートル、地上階に約1000平方メートルのアリアガ・アトリウムを新設（ArchDaily）
事業費は4500万ユーロ（The Art Newspaper）。アトリウムの中心には、作曲家アリアガに捧げたフランシスコ・ドゥリオの彫刻噴水が置かれ、1945年の旧館正面入口も復元された

hojosen.title: 既存に触れない増築
hojosen.body: 歴史的建物の増築では、既存躯体に新しい荷重をかけず、独立した構造で支える手法が広がっています。既存の耐震性能や基礎の余力を精査する必要がなく、将来の撤去も容易になる一方、独立柱を立てる敷地の余白が必要です。日本でも美術館や庁舎の増築で同様の判断が増えています。

hojosen.title: ビルバオと建築
hojosen.body: ビルバオは1997年のグッゲンハイム美術館（フランク・ゲーリー設計）で産業都市から観光都市へ転換した「ビルバオ効果」の代名詞です。フォスターは同市の地下鉄駅（1995年）も設計しており、今回の美術館増築は同じ建築家が30年を経て市の中心部に再び関わる事例でもあります。

en.title: Foster + Partners' Agravitas extension floats a 55 m gallery over Bilbao's Fine Arts Museum
en.summary: The Bilbao Fine Arts Museum in northern Spain reopened on Oct 6 after an extension designed by Foster + Partners. Large V-shaped columns hold a 55 m (180 ft) gallery up in the air above the existing buildings.
body: The Bilbao Fine Arts Museum in Bilbao, northern Spain, reopened on Oct 6 after four years of construction. It was designed by Foster + Partners with local architect Luis María Uriarte. The extension is named Agravitas, meaning “without gravity.” According to Dezeen, a 55 m (180 ft) bridge-like gallery is held up by large V-shaped columns and spans over the existing complex without touching its structure.

According to ArchDaily, the new steel structure increases the existing building's floor area by 60%, adding 2,300 m² (24,800 sq ft) of flexible exhibition space on two levels, along with space for education programs, workshops and offices. Lifting the new volume up frees the ground level, creating the Arriaga Atrium of about 1,000 m² (10,800 sq ft). The steel was sourced locally, a nod to Bilbao's industrial history.

The Art Newspaper reports the project cost at €45 million. Entry is free for the first week after the reopening, and the main entrance of the red-brick original building, completed in 1945, has been restored and brought back into use. Bilbao is best known for Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Museum, but this is an older institution founded in 1908, with a collection ranging from classical Spanish painting to modern and contemporary Basque art.
en.commentary: Floating a 55 m (180 ft) box over an existing museum. As a way to extend a building, that's pretty bold. Normally you add onto the side or the back of an old building, right? But the Bilbao Fine Arts Museum faces a park in the center of the city, and there was no land to spread out sideways. So Foster chose to build upward, and on top of that, put no load on the existing buildings. V-shaped columns stand beside the existing wings, and a steel bridge spans across them. That's why the extension looks like it's floating, and it also meant the old building didn't have to be torn down during construction. What I find interesting is that this structural choice becomes the way the architecture looks. The structural decision not to lean on the old building turned into the name “without gravity.” And the ground freed up by lifting the gallery has come back to the public as a 1,000 m² (10,800 sq ft) atrium. In Japan, too, plenty of museums and government buildings are struggling with how to extend or rebuild. Next time you see an extension to an old public building, look for the columns and find where the new part carries its weight.
briefing: Designed by Foster + Partners and Luis María Uriarte. Construction began in November 2022, and after about four years of work a ceremony was held on Oct 5, 2026, followed by the public opening on Oct 6. Entry is free through Oct 13 (Dezeen, local reports)

The extension is a bridge-like structure made of steel from Bilbao, supported on V-shaped columns without touching the existing structure. It adds 2,300 m² (24,800 sq ft) of exhibition space on two levels and a new Arriaga Atrium of about 1,000 m² (10,800 sq ft) at ground level (ArchDaily)

The project cost €45 million (The Art Newspaper). At the center of the atrium stands Francisco Durrio's sculptural fountain dedicated to the composer Arriaga, and the main entrance of the 1945 old building has been restored

hojosen.title: Extensions that leave the old alone
hojosen.body: In extensions to historic buildings, a growing approach is to carry the new part on its own independent structure without adding load to the existing one. There is no need to closely assess the old building's seismic performance or spare foundation capacity, and the addition is easier to remove in the future, but the site needs room for the independent columns. In Japan, too, more museums and government buildings are making the same choice for their extensions.

hojosen.title: Bilbao and architecture
hojosen.body: Bilbao is synonymous with the “Bilbao effect,” its shift from industrial city to tourist destination after the Guggenheim Museum, designed by Frank Gehry, opened in 1997. Foster also designed the city's metro stations (1995), so this museum extension is a case of the same architect returning to the heart of the city 30 years later.
